\begin{definition}\label{KLprop}
Let $\Phi:\mathbb R^d\to \bar{\mathbb R}$  be a proper  lower semicontinuous function.
We say that $\Phi$ has the Kurdyka-{\L}ojasiewicz (K{\L}) property at 
$x^*\in {\rm dom} \;\partial \Phi$ if there exists a neighborhood $U$ of $x^*$, 
$\eta\in(0,\infty)$ and a continuous concave function $\psi\in\Psi_{\eta}$ such that
%
\begin{eqnarray}\label{KLine}
\psi'\big(\Phi(x)-\Phi(x^*)\big) {\rm dist}\big(0,\partial \Phi(x)\big)\ge 1.
\end{eqnarray}
 If $\Phi$ satisfies the  property at each point of $ {\rm dom} \;\partial \Phi$, then $\Phi$ is a 
{K\L} function. 
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}\label{KLset}
Let $\Phi:\mathbb R^d\to \bar{\mathbb R}$  be a proper  lower semicontinuous function that
 takes constant value on $\Omega$ and satisfies the {K\L} property at each point of $\Omega$.
We say $\Phi$ satisfies a K{\L} property on $\Omega$ if there exists
$\epsilon>0$, $\eta>0$, and $\psi\in\Psi_{\eta}$ such that 
for every $x^*\in\Omega$ and every element $x$ belongs to the intersection
$ \{x\in\mathbb R^d: {\rm dist} (x,\Omega)<\epsilon\} \cap [\Phi(x^*) <\Phi(x) <   \Phi(x^*)+\eta],$
 (\ref{KLine}) holds. 
 \end{definition}

\begin{lemma}
Let $\Phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ be Fr\'echet differentiable such that 
its gradient is Lipschitz continuous with constant $L_{\Phi}>0$. Then 
for every $u,v\in\mathbb R^d$ and every $\xi\in[u,v]=\{(1-t)u+tv:\;t\in[0,1]\}$
it holds 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{Lip}
\Phi(v)\le \Phi(u)+\langle \nabla \Phi(\xi),v-u\rangle +\frac{L_{\Phi}}{2}\|v-u\|^2.
\end{eqnarray}

\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let $u, v\in\mathbb R^d$, and $\xi=(1-t)u+tv$ for $t\in [0,1]$. Then we have
%
\begin{eqnarray*}
&\Phi(v) -\Phi(u) = \int_0^1 \langle \nabla \Phi((1-r) u+rv), v-u \rangle dr &\\
&=  \int_0^1  \langle \nabla \Phi((1-r) u+rv)-\nabla \Phi(\xi), v-u \rangle dr
+\langle \nabla \Phi(\xi) , v-u\rangle. &
\end{eqnarray*}

Since $\Phi$ has Lipschitz continuous gradients with constant $L_{\Phi}>0$, then we have
\begin{eqnarray*}
&|\Phi(v) -\Phi(u) - \langle \nabla \Phi(\xi) , v-u\rangle|
=\Big| \int_0^1  \langle \nabla \Phi((1-r) u+rv)-\nabla \Phi(\xi), v-u \rangle dr\Big | 
&\\
&
\le  \int_0^1  \Big\|  \nabla \Phi((1-r) u+rv)-\nabla \Phi(\xi)\Big\|\cdot \Big\|v-u\Big \|dr 
\le  L_{\Phi} \|v-u\|^2 \int_0^1 |r-t| dr
& \\ &
=  L_{\Phi} 
\|v-u\|^2 \Big( \int_0^t (-r+t) dr + \int_t^1 (r-t) dr \Big)
& \\&
=  L_{\Phi} \Big(\frac 12 -t(1-t)\Big) \|v-u\|^2 
\le \frac {L_{\Phi}}{2}\|v-u\|^2.\quad  \square &
\end{eqnarray*}


\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{thm-d}
{(Subgradient bound)} Let $\{({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k)\}_{k\ge 0}$ be a sequence generated by the PADMM
 algorithm (\ref{padmm}). Then there exists 
$d^{k}:=\big(\{d^{k}_{x_i}\}_{i=1}^p,d^{k}_y,d^{k}_z\big)\in\partial \mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k})$ and  a constant $\rho>0$
such that 
%
\begin{eqnarray}\label{nd}
|||d^{k}||| &\le&
 \rho \Big(\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k}\|+ \|\Delta y^{k}\|+ \|\Delta z^{k}\|\Big), 
\end{eqnarray}
%
where %
\begin{eqnarray}\label{rho}
\rho:=\max\Big\{
\|{\bf Q}\|+\|{\bf A}\|^2,\;\;\;
\|P\|+
\alpha \|{\bf A}\|\|B\|
, \;\;\;
\|{\bf A}\|  +\|B\|+\frac{1}{\alpha\beta}\Big\},
\end{eqnarray}
%
$\|{\bf Q}\|:=\sum_{i=1}^p\|Q_i\|$ and $\|{\bf A}\|:=\sum_{i=1}^p\|A_i\|$,
and for any sequence $\{u^k\}_{k\ge 0}$,
$\Delta u^{k+1}=u^{k+1}-u^k$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let $k\ge 1$ be fixed. By the optimality condition of the $x_i$ subproblem
of PADMM algorithm for 
$i=1,\dots, p$ we have
%
\begin{eqnarray*}
-A_i\tr z^{k-1}
-\alpha A_i\tr (A_{<i}x_{<i}^{k}+A_ix_i^{k}+A_{>i}x_{>i}^{k-1}+By^{k-1}+b)
-Q_i\Delta x_i^{k}
\in\partial f_i(x_i^{k}).
\end{eqnarray*}
%
Taking partial differential of $\mathcal L^{\alpha}$ with respect to $x_i$
and evaluating the result at the point $({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k})$ yields
\[
\partial_{x_i} \mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k})=
\partial f_i(x_i^{k})+A_i\tr z^{k}+
\alpha A_i\tr \big({\bf Ax}^{k}+By^{k}+ b\big).
\]
%
Therefore 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{dxinL}
\begin{array}{lll}
d_{x_i}^{k}:=
A_i\tr \Delta z^{k}+
\alpha A_i\tr A_{>i}\Delta x_{>i}^{k}
+\alpha A_i\tr B\Delta y^{k}
-Q_i\Delta x_i^{k}
\in \partial_{x_i} \mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k}).
\end{array}
 \end{eqnarray}
%
The optimality criterion of $y$ subproblem gives
\[
\nabla h(y^{k})=-B\tr z^{k-1}- \alpha B\tr ({\bf A x}^{k}+By^{k}+b) 
- {P} \Delta y^{k}.
\]
By taking partial differential of $\mathcal L^{\alpha}$ with respect to $y$
and evaluating it at $({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k}) $ we obtain
\[
\nabla_y \mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k}) =
\nabla h(y^{k})+B\tr z^{k}+\alpha B\tr \big({\bf Ax}^{k}+By^{k}+b\big).
\]
The last two equations follow that
\begin{eqnarray}\label{dyinL}
d_y^{k}:=B\tr \Delta z^{k}- P \Delta y^{k}
= \nabla_y \mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k}).
\end{eqnarray}
%
Lastly, by the $z$ subproblem we have ${\bf Ax}^{k}+By^{k}+b=\frac{1}{\alpha\beta}
 \Delta z^k$ hence 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{dzinL}
d_z^{k}:=\frac{1}{\alpha\beta}
 \Delta z^{k}= \nabla_z \mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k}).
\end{eqnarray}
Hence, by (\ref{dxinL}), (\ref{dyinL}), , and (\ref{dzinL}), we 
 have 
$
d^{k}:=\big(\{d^{k}_{x_i}\}_{i=1}^p,d^{k}_y,d^{k}_z\big)\in\partial \mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k}).
$
%
By the norm property we have $\|d_z^{k}\|=\frac{1}{\alpha\beta} \|\Delta z^{k}\|$ 
and by the  triangle inequality from (\ref{dxinL}) and (\ref{dyinL}) we obtain 
%
\begin{eqnarray*} \label{ndx}
&\|d_{x_i}^{k}\|\le
\|A_i\|\|\Delta z^{k}\|+\alpha \|A_i\|\Big({\sum_{j=i+1}^p}\|A_j\|\|\Delta x_j^{k}\|\Big)
+\alpha\|A_i\|\|B\|\|\Delta y^{k}\|+\|Q_i\|\|\Delta x_i^{k}\|, &\\
%
&\|d_y^{k}\|\le\|B\| \|\Delta z^{k}\| +\|P\| \|\Delta y^{k}\|. &
%\|d_z^{k}\|=\frac{1}{\alpha\beta} \|\Delta z^{k}\|.
\end{eqnarray*}
%
Hence we get
%
\begin{eqnarray*}
&|||d^{k}||| \le  \sum_{i=1}^p\|d_{x_i}^{k}\|+ \|d_y^{k}\|+\|d_z^{k}\|
\le \sum_{i=1}^p \|Q_i\|\|\Delta x_i^{k}\|
+ \sum_{i=2}^p \|A_i\| \|\Delta x_i^{k}\|\sum_{j=1}^{i-1}\|A_j\| 
& \\&
+\Big(\|P\|+\alpha\|B\|\sum_{i=1}^p \|A_i\|  \Big)      \|\Delta y^{k}\|
+\Big( \sum_{i=1}^p \|A_i\|  +\|B\|+\frac{1}{\alpha\beta}\Big)       \|\Delta z^{k}\|
&\\&
\le 
\Big(\|{\bf Q}\|+\|{\bf A}\|^2\Big) \sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k}\|
+\Big(\|P\|+\alpha \|{\bf A}\| \|B\| \Big)      \|\Delta y^{k}\|
+\Big(\|{\bf A}\|  +\|B\|+\frac{1}{\alpha\beta}\Big)  \|\Delta z^{k}\|
&\\&
\le \rho \Big( \sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k}\|+   \|\Delta y^{k}\|+  \|\Delta z^{k}\|\Big).
\quad\square &
\end{eqnarray*}
%
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{thm-cluster}
{(Limiting continuity)} 
Suppose that A1-A2  hold. 
If $({\bf x}^*, y^*, z^*)$ is the limit point of $\{({\bf x}^{k_j},y^{k_j},z^{k_j})\}_{j\ge 0}$, a subsequence of 
$\{{\bf x}^k, y^k, z^k\}_{k\ge 0}$ generated by the PADMM algorithm (\ref{padmm}). Then 
$ \mathcal L^{\alpha} ({\bf x}^*, y^*, z^*)=\lim_{j\to\infty} \mathcal L^{\alpha} ({\bf x}^{k_j},y^{k_j},z^{k_j}).
$
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let $\{({\bf x}^{k_j},y^{k_j},z^{k_j})\}_{j\ge 0}$ be a subsequence of the sequence 
$\{({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k})\}_{j\ge 0}$
generated by the PADMM algorithm such that
$\lim_{j\to\infty} ({\bf x}^{k_j},y^{k_j},z^{k_j})=({\bf x}^*, y^*, z^*).$
By A1, for $i=1,\dots,p$ the functions $f_i$ are lower semicontinuous hence

\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:flsc0}
f_i(x_i^*)\le \lim\inf_{j\to\infty} f(x_i^{k_j}).
\end{eqnarray}
%
By the $x_i$-subproblem of the PADMM algorithm for any $v\in\mathbb R^{n_i}$ we have 
\[
\mathcal L^{\alpha} (x_{<i}^{k_j+1},x_i^{k_j+1}, x^{k_j}_{>i}, y^{k_j},z^{k_j})+
\frac{1}{2}\|\Delta x_i^{k_j+1}\|_{Q_i}^2
\le \mathcal L^{\alpha} (x_{<i}^{k_j+1},v, x^{k_j}_{>i}, y^{k_j},z^{k_j})
+\frac{1}{2}\|v- x_i^{k_j}\|_{Q_i}^2.
\]
We choose $v=x_i^*$ and exploit the cosine rule
$\|a_1+c\|^2-\|a_2+c\|^2=\|a_2-a_1\|^2+2\langle a_2+c, a_2-a_1\rangle$
with 
$a_1=A_ix_i^*$, $a_2=A_ix_i^{k_j+1}$ 
and $c=A_{<i}x_{<i}^{k_j+1}+A_{>i}x^{k_j}_{>i}+By^{k_j}+b$ to obtain
 %
\begin{eqnarray*}
&f_i(x_i^{k_j+1})- f_i(x_i^*) +
\langle A_i\tr z^{k_j},x^{k_j+1}_i-x_i^*\rangle+\|\Delta x_i^{k_j+1}\|^2_{Q_i} 
\le 
\frac{\alpha}{2}\|A_i (x_i^{k_j+1}-x_i^*)\|^2&
\\
&+\alpha \Big\langle A_i (x_i^*-x_i^{k_j+1}), A_{<i}x^{k_j+1}_{<i}+A_ix_i^{k_j+1}+A_{>i}x_{>i}^{k_j}+By^{k_j}+b\Big\rangle.
&
\end{eqnarray*}
%
Since $\{({\bf x}^{k_j},y^{k_j},z^{k_j})\}_{j\ge 0}$  is a convergent sequence, 
 it is bounded and the difference of consequtive terms approaches  zero. 
Thus the latter inequality reduces to 
$\displaystyle{\lim\sup_{j\to \infty}} f_i(x_i^{k_j+1})-f_i(x_i^*)\le 0$ and 
in view of (\ref{eq:flsc0}) we then have
$
\lim_{j\to \infty} f_i(x_i^{k_j})=f_i(x_i^*),
$
which follows that
$
\lim_{j\to \infty} \sum_{i=1}^p f_i(x_i^{k_j})=\sum_{i=1}^p f_i(x_i^*).
$
%
By A2, $h(y)$ is smooth hence $\lim_{j\to\infty} h(y^{k_j})= h(y^*)$.
Clearly, ${\bf Ax}^{k_j}+By^{k_j}+b\to {\bf Ax}^{*}+By^{*}+b$
as $j\to\infty$.
Thus $\displaystyle{\lim_{j\to\infty}} \mathcal L^{\alpha} ({\bf x}^{k_j},y^{k_j},z^{k_j})
= \mathcal L^{\alpha} ({\bf x}^*, y^*, z^*).$ $\quad\square$
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{thm-cluster0}
{(Limit point is critical point)} The set of limit points of the sequence
$\{({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k)\}_{k\ge 0}$ generated by the PADMM algorithm (\ref{padmm}),
denoted 
$\omega\big(\{({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k)\}_{k\ge 0}\big)$, satisfies
\[
\omega\big( \{ ({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k) \}_{k\ge 0} \big) \subseteq {\rm crit} \;\mathcal L^{\alpha}
:=
\left\{
({\bf x}^*,y^*,z^*):
\begin{array}{l}
 0\in\partial f_i(x_i^*)+A_i\tr z^*,\; i=1,\dots, p\\
\nabla h(y^*)+ B\tr z^*=0,\\
{\bf Ax}^*+By^*+b=0
\end{array}
\right\},
\]
where ${\rm crit}\;\mathcal L^{\alpha}$ denotes the set of critical points of $\mathcal L^{\alpha}$.
%
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let $(\hat {\bf x}, \hat y, \hat z)\in \omega\big( \{ ({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k) \}_{k\ge 0} \big)$,
hence there exists a subsequence $\{({\bf x}^{k_j},y^{k_j},z^{k_j})\}_{j\ge 0}$
of $\{({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k)\}_{k\ge 0}$ such that 
$\lim_{j\to\infty} ({\bf x}^{k_j},y^{k_j},z^{k_j})=(\hat {\bf x}, \hat y, \hat z).$
For the sequence $\{d^k\}_{k\ge 0}$, we have $d^{k_j}\in\partial \mathcal L^{\alpha}(x^{k_j}, y^{k_j}, z^{k_j})$
for $j\ge 1$ and $d^{k_j}\to 0$ as $j\to \infty$ while $({\bf x}^{k_j}, y^{k_j}, z^{k_j})\to (\hat {\bf x}, \hat y,\hat z)$
and $\displaystyle{\lim_{j\to\infty}} \mathcal L^{\alpha} ({\bf x}^{k_j},y^{k_j},z^{k_j})
= \mathcal L^{\alpha} (\hat {\bf x}, \hat y, \hat z).$
 By the closeness criterion of the limiting sub-differential 
we then have $0\in \partial \mathcal L^{\alpha}(\hat{\bf x}, \hat{y}, \hat {z})$,
and equivalently, $(\hat{\bf x}, \hat{y}, \hat {z})\in {\rm crit} (\mathcal L^{\alpha})$.
 $\square$
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}{(bound dual)}\label{bounddual}
Suppose that A2 and A3 hold.
%\[
%\rho(\beta):=1-|1-\beta|,
%\quad 
%c_1:=  \frac{1}{\alpha\rho(\beta)\lambda_{++}^{B\tr B}},
%\quad
%c_2:=  \frac{2\beta}{\alpha\rho(\beta)^2\lambda_{++}^{B\tr B}}.
%\]
%where  $\lambda_{++}^{B\tr B}$ be the smallest 
%strictly-positive eigenvalue of $B\tr B$.
%
Then for all $k\in\mathbb Z_+$ the following assertions are true.
\begin{itemize}
%
\item [(i)] $B\tr z^{k}=\beta w^{k}+(1-\beta) B\tr z^{k-1},$ where 
$w^{k}=-P\Delta y^{k}-\nabla h(y^{k}),$
%
\item [(ii)]
$\frac{1}{\alpha\beta}\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|^2
\le c_4 \|\Delta y^{k+1}\|^2
+c_3 \|\Delta y^{k}\|^2+c_5 \|B\tr \Delta z^{k}\|^2
-c_5\| B\tr \Delta z^{k+1}\|^2$,
%
\item [(iii)]
$\frac{1}{2\alpha}\|z^{k+1}\|^2\le c_1  \|P\|^2 \|\Delta y^{k+1}\|^2
+ c_1 \|\nabla h(y^{k+1})\|^2
+c_6\|B\tr \Delta z^{k+1}\|^2$,
\end{itemize}
where $c_i$, $i=2,\dots,6$ are defined in (\ref{quantities}).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
{\bf (i)} 
By the the optimality condition of $y$-subproblem we have
\[
\alpha B\tr ({\bf Ax}^{k}+By^{k}+b)+B\tr z^{k-1}-w^k=0
\]
which together with the $z$-iterate ${\bf Ax}^{k}+By^{k}+b=\frac{1}{\alpha\beta}(z^k-z^{k-1})$ we obtain the result.


{\bf (ii)} By A3 and the $z$ iterate of the PADMM algorithm we have $\Delta z^{k+1}\in {\rm Im}(B)$, thus 
 $\lambda_{++}^{B\tr B}\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|^2\le \|B\tr \Delta z^{k+1}\|^2$.
Part (i) follows 
$B\tr \Delta z^{k+1}=\beta\Delta w^{k+1}+(1-\beta) B\tr \Delta z^{k}$ and 
equivalently 
%
\begin{eqnarray*}
B\tr \Delta z^{k+1}=\rho(\beta)
\Big(\frac{\beta\Delta w^{k+1}}{\rho(\beta)} \Big)
+|1-\beta| \Big({\rm sign}(1-\beta) B\tr \Delta z^k\Big),
\end{eqnarray*}
where ${\rm sign} (\lambda)=1$ if $\lambda\ge 0$ and ${\rm sign} (\lambda)=-1$ if $\lambda<0$.
By $\rho(\beta)+|1-\beta|=1$ and the convexity of $\|\cdot\|^2$ 
we have
%
\begin{eqnarray}\label{gg}
\|B\tr \Delta z^{k+1}\|^2
\le  \frac{\beta^2}{\rho(\beta)}  \|\Delta w^{k+1}\|^2
+|1-\beta| \|B\tr \Delta z^{k}\|^2.%-|1-\beta| \Big\| B^*\Delta z^{k+1}\Big\|^2.
\end{eqnarray}
This also follows that 
%
\begin{eqnarray*}\label{gg}
\rho(\beta)\lambda_{++}^{B\tr B} \|\Delta z^{k+1}\|^2&\le& \rho(\beta)\|B\tr \Delta z^{k+1}\|^2\\
%
&\le&  \frac{\beta^2}{\rho(\beta)}  \|\Delta w^{k+1}\|^2
+|1-\beta| \|B\tr \Delta z^{k}\|^2-|1-\beta| \| B\tr \Delta z^{k+1}\|^2.
\end{eqnarray*}
%
Rearrange this to obtain
%
\begin{eqnarray}\label{gg}
\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|^2\le
 \frac{\beta^2}{\rho(\beta)^2\lambda_{++}^{B\tr B} }  \|\Delta w^{k+1}\|^2
+\frac{|1-\beta|}{\rho(\beta)\lambda_{++}^{B\tr B} } \|B\tr \Delta z^{k}\|^2
-\frac{|1-\beta|}{\rho(\beta)\lambda_{++}^{B\tr B} } \| B\tr \Delta z^{k+1}\|^2.
\end{eqnarray}
%
By the optimality condition of $y$ subproblem we have 
\[
\Delta w^{k+1}=-P\Delta y^{k+1}+P\Delta y^k+\nabla h(y^{k})-\nabla h(y^{k+1}).
\]
By $\|a+b\|^2\le 2\|a\|^2+2\|b\|^2$ and the fact that $\nabla h$ has $L_h$ Lipschitz gradients
we obtain
\[
\|\Delta w^{k+1}\|^2\le 2(\|P\|+L_h)^2\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|^2+2\|P\|^2 \|\Delta y^k\|^2.
\]
Exploit this in (\ref{gg}) to get
\begin{eqnarray*}\label{gg0}
\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|^2&\le&
 \frac{2\beta^2 (\|P\|+L_h)^2}{\rho(\beta)^2\lambda_{++}^{B\tr B} }          \|\Delta y^{k+1}\|^2
 + \frac{2\beta^2\|P\|^2}{\rho(\beta)^2\lambda_{++}^{B\tr B} }    \|\Delta y^k\|^2\\
 &&+\frac{|1-\beta|}{\rho(\beta)\lambda_{++}^{B\tr B} } \|B\tr \Delta z^{k}\|^2
-\frac{|1-\beta|}{\rho(\beta)\lambda_{++}^{B\tr B} } \| B\tr \Delta z^{k+1}\|^2.
\end{eqnarray*}
We divide both sides by $\alpha\beta$ to get 
%
\begin{eqnarray*}
\frac{1}{\alpha\beta}\Big\|\Delta z^{k+1}\Big\|^2
\le c_4 \Big\|\Delta y^{k+1}\Big\|^2
+c_3 \|\Delta y^{k}\|^2+c_5 \Big\|B\tr \Delta z^{k}\Big\|^2
-c_5 \Big\| B\tr \Delta z^{k+1}\Big\|^2.
\end{eqnarray*}

{\bf (iii).} By part (i) we have
%
$\beta B\tr z^{k+1}=\beta w^{k+1}+(1-\beta) B\tr (z^k-z^{k+1})$ 
which can be written equivalently as follows
%
\begin{eqnarray*}
\beta B\tr z^{k+1}= \rho(\beta)\cdot \frac{\beta w^{k+1}}{\rho(\beta)}
+|1-\beta|\cdot {\rm sign}(1-\beta) B\tr (z^k-z^{k+1}).
\end{eqnarray*}
By $\rho(\beta)+|1-\beta|=1$ and the convexity of $\|\cdot\|^2$
we get
%
\begin{eqnarray*}
\beta^2\lambda_{++}^{B\tr B} \|z^{k+1}\|^2
\le   \beta^2 \|B\tr z^{k+1}\|^2
\le
\rho(\beta)\cdot \Big\| \frac{\beta w^{k+1}}{\rho(\beta)}\Big\|^2
+|1-\beta| \|B\tr \Delta z^{k+1}\|^2.
\end{eqnarray*}
%
Simplify and rearrange to get
%
\begin{eqnarray*}
\|z^{k+1}\|^2
\le 
\frac{1}{\rho(\beta)\lambda_{++}^{B\tr B}}      \|w^{k+1}\|^2
+\frac{|1-\beta|}{\beta^2 \lambda_{++}^{B\tr B}      } \|B\tr \Delta z^{k+1}\|^2.
\end{eqnarray*}
%
Exploit $\|w^{k+1}\|^2\le 2 \|P\|^2 \|\Delta y^{k+1}\|^2+2\|\nabla h(y^{k+1})\|^2$
to obtain 
%
\begin{eqnarray*}
\|z^{k+1}\|^2
\le
\frac{2\|P\|^2}{\rho(\beta)\lambda_{++}^{B\tr B}}  \|\Delta y^{k+1}\|^2
+ \frac{2}{\rho(\beta)\lambda_{++}^{B\tr B}} \|\nabla h(y^{k+1})\|^2
+\frac{|1-\beta|}{\beta^2\lambda_{++}^{B\tr B}} \|B\tr \Delta z^{k+1}\|^2.
\end{eqnarray*}
%
Divide both sides by $2\alpha$ to obtain the result.
This concludes the proof.  $\square$
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{chgL}
{(change of $\mathcal L^{\alpha}$ during each variable update)} 
Suppose that A1-A4 hold. The iterates in PADMM algorithm (\ref{padmm}) satisfy
%
\begin{itemize}
\item [(i)] $\mathcal L^{\alpha}(x_{<i}^{k+1},x_i^k, x^{k}_{>i},y^k,z^k)-
\mathcal L^{\alpha}(x_{<i}^{k+1},x_i^{k+1}, x^{k}_{>i},y^k,z^k)\ge \frac{1}{2} \|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|_{T_i}^2$ where
$T_i=Q_i$ or $T_i=\alpha A_i\tr A_i-\epsilon_i I$ where $\epsilon_i >0$ defined in A4 for $i=1,\dots, p$.
%
\item [(ii)]
$\mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^{k+1},y^k, z^k)-\mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^{k+1},y^{k+1},z^{k})
\ge \frac{1}{2} \|\Delta y^{k+1}\|_D^2$, where $D$ is defined in (\ref{quantities}).
\item [(iii)] $\mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^{k+1},y^{k+1}, z^k)-
\mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^{k+1},y^{k+1},z^{k+1})=-\frac{1}{\alpha\beta}\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|^2.$
%
\end{itemize}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
{\bf (i)} Let $k\in\mathbb Z_+$ and $i\in\{1,\dots,p\}$ be fixed.
By the $x_i$ subproblem we have
\[
\mathcal L^{\alpha}(x_{<i}^{k+1},x_i^{k}, x^{k}_{>i},y^k,z^k)-
\mathcal L^{\alpha}(x_{<i}^{k+1},x_i^{k+1}, x^{k}_{>i},y^k,z^k)
\ge \|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|_{Q_i}^2.
\]
%
On the other hand, by the optimality condition of $x_i$-sub-minimization problem we have 
$ \bar{d_i}\in\partial f_i(x_i^{k+1})$
where 
\[
\bar{d_i}:=-A_i \tr z^k-
\alpha A_i\tr \big(A_{<i} x_{<i}^{k+1}+A_ix_i^{k+1}+A_{>i}x_{>i}^k+By^k+b
\big).
\]
By this we then have
\begin{eqnarray*}
&\mathcal L^{\alpha}(x_{<i}^{k+1},x_i^k, x^{k}_{>i},y^k,z^k)-
\mathcal L^{\alpha}(x_{<i}^{k+1},x_i^{k+1}, x^{k}_{>i},y^k,z^k)& \\[.1in]
&=f_i(x_i^k)-f_i(x_i^{k+1})
+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|A_i\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|^2-\langle \bar{d_i}, \Delta x_i^{k+1}\rangle&
\\[.1in]
&\ge \frac{\alpha}{2}\|A_i\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|^2
- \frac{\epsilon_i}{2}\|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|^2
=\frac 12 \|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|_{\alpha A_i\tr A_i-\epsilon_iI}^2.&
\end{eqnarray*}

%%%%
{\bf (ii)}
Let $k\ge 0$ be fixed. From the optimality condition of $y$ minimization problem 
we have
\begin{eqnarray*}
\nabla h(y^{k+1})+\alpha B\tr ({\bf Ax}^{k+1}+By^{k+1}+b)
+B\tr z^k+P \Delta y^{k+1}=0.
\end{eqnarray*}
Multiply this equation by $\Delta y^{k+1}$ and rearrange to obtain
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:2}
- \alpha\big\langle B\tr ({\bf Ax}^{k+1}+ By^{k+1}+b),\Delta y^{k+1}\big\rangle 
-\langle B\tr z^k, \Delta y^{k+1}\rangle
=\langle \nabla h(y^{k+1}),\Delta y^{k+1}\rangle +\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|_P^2.
\end{eqnarray}
By this and the fact that $h(y)$ is $L_h$ Lipschitz continuous we then get 
%
\begin{eqnarray*}
&\mathcal L^{\alpha}(x^{k+1},y^k,z^k)-\mathcal L^{\alpha}(x^{k+1},y^{k+1},z^{k})&
\\[.1in]
&= h(y^k)-h(y^{k+1})
+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|{\bf Ax}^{k+1}+By^k+b\|^2
-\frac{\alpha}{2}\|{\bf Ax}^{k+1}+By^{k+1}+b\|^2
-\langle B\tr z^k, \Delta y^{k+1} \rangle&
\\[.1in]
 &=h(y^k)-h(y^{k+1})
+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|B\Delta y^{k+1}\|^2
-\alpha \langle \Delta y^{k+1}, B\tr ({\bf Ax}^{k+1}+By^{k+1}+b)\rangle 
-\langle B\tr z^k, \Delta y^{k+1} \rangle&
\\[.1in]
&=h(y^k)-h(y^{k+1})
+\langle \nabla h(y^{k+1}),\Delta y^{k+1}\rangle +\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|_P^2
+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|B\Delta y^{k+1}\|^2
&\\[.1in]
&\ge\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|_P^2
+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|B\Delta y^{k+1}\|^2
-\frac{L_h}{2}\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|^2 = 
\frac{1}{2} \|\Delta y^{k+1}\|_{D}^2.&
\end{eqnarray*}
%
%
{\bf (iii)} By the $z$ iterate of the algorithm we obtain
\begin{eqnarray*}
&\mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^{k+1},y^{k+1}, z^k)-
\mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^{k+1},y^{k+1},z^{k+1})=
\langle z^k-z^{k+1}, {\bf Ax}^{k+1}+By^{k+1}+b\rangle
=-\frac{1}{\alpha\beta}\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|^2.&
\end{eqnarray*}
%
That completes the proof. $\square$
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:chgLiter}
{(change of $\mathcal L^{\alpha}$ after each iteration)} 
We assume that A1-A4 hold.
The iterates in PADMM algorithm (\ref{padmm}) satisfy
%
\begin{eqnarray}\label{chgLiter}
\begin{array}{c}
\mathcal L^{\alpha}\big({\bf x}^{k+1},y^{k+1},z^{k+1}\big)
+\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|_{T_i}^2
+ \frac{1}{2} \|\Delta y^{k+1}\|_{D-2\epsilon_0c_4 I_m}^2\\[.1in]
+\displaystyle{\frac{\epsilon_0-1}{\alpha\beta}}\big\|\Delta z^{k+1}\big\|^2
+\epsilon_0c_5 \big\|B\tr \Delta z^{k+1}\big\|^2
\le  \mathcal L^{\alpha}\big(x^{k},y^k,z^k\big)+
\epsilon_0c_5 \big\|B\tr \Delta z^k\big\|^2
+\epsilon_0c_3 \big\|\Delta y^k\big\|^2,
\end{array}
\end{eqnarray}
where $\epsilon_0>1$, and $c_3,c_4,c_5$ are defined in (\ref{quantities}).
%
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
By Lemma \ref{chgL} we have 
\begin{eqnarray*}
&\mathcal L^{\alpha}(x^{k+1},y^{k+1},z^{k+1})=\mathcal L^{\alpha}(x^{k+1},y^{k+1},z^{k}) 
+ \frac{1}{\alpha\beta}\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|^2
&\\[.1in]&
\le  \mathcal L^{\alpha}(x^{k+1},y^{k},z^{k}) + \frac{1}{\alpha\beta}\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|^2
-\frac{1}{2} \|\Delta y^{k+1}\|_{D}^2 
&\\[.1in]&
\le \mathcal L^{\alpha}(x^{k},y^{k},z^{k})
+ \frac{1}{\alpha\beta}\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|^2
-\frac{1}{2} \|\Delta y^{k+1}\|_{D}^2 -\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^p \|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|^2_{T_i}.&
\end{eqnarray*}
By Lemma \ref{bounddual} for $\epsilon_0>1$ we have 
\[
\frac{\epsilon_0}{\alpha\beta}\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|^2
\le\epsilon_0c_4 \|\Delta y^{k+1}\|^2
+\epsilon_0c_3 \|\Delta y^{k}\|^2+
\epsilon_0c_5 \|B\tr \Delta z^{k}\|^2
-\epsilon_0c_5\| B\tr \Delta z^{k+1}\|^2.
\]
Add this to the latter inequality and rearrange to obtain (\ref{chgLiter}). $\square$
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{thm1}
%{\bf (monotonicity/convergence of $\bar{\mathcal L}$)}
Suppose that A1-A4 hold, and 
\[
\bar\tau =\min\{ \max \{ q_i,\lambda_{++}^{\alpha A_i\tr A_i-\epsilon_i I} \} : i=1,\dots, p\}.
\]
 If $\sigma=\min\{\lambda_{\min}(\bar D), \bar\tau,\frac{\epsilon_0-1}{\alpha\beta}\}>0$ where 
 $\bar D$ is defined in (\ref{quantities}), then
the following assertions hold.
%
\begin{itemize}
\item [(i)] The sequence $\{\bar {\mathcal L_k}\}_{k\ge 1}$ is monotonically decreasing and 
%
\begin{eqnarray}\label{Lbarmon}
\bar{\mathcal L}_{k+1}+\sigma
\big[\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|^2
+ \|\Delta y^{k+1}\|^2+
\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|^2\big]
\le \bar{\mathcal L}_k.
\end{eqnarray}
%
%
\item [(ii)] If the sequence $\{{\bf x}^k, y^k, z^k\}_{k\ge 0}$ generated by the PADMM is bounded 
then $\bar{\mathcal L}_k$ is bounded from below for all $k \in \mathbb N$  and converges as $k$ approaches infinity.
%%
%\item [(iii)] If $B\tr B$ is invertible, then $\{{\bf x}^k, y^k, z^k\}_{k\ge 0}$ is bounded.
%\item [(iv)]  If $\{{\bf x}^k, y^k, z^k\}_{k\ge 0}$ is bounded
%then 
%$\lim_{k\to \infty} \|\Delta x_i^{k}\|=\lim_{k\to \infty} \|\Delta y^{k}\|=\lim_{k\to \infty} \|\Delta z^{k}\|=0.$
\end{itemize}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
{\bf (i)} By (\ref{chgLiter}) and (\ref{Lbark}) we obtain 
\[
\bar{\mathcal L}_{k+1}
+\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^p \|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|^2_{T_i}
+\frac 12\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|^2_{D-2\epsilon_0(c_3+c_4)}+
\displaystyle{\frac{\epsilon_0-1}{\alpha\beta}}\big\|\Delta z^{k+1}\big\|^2
\le \bar{\mathcal L}_k.
\]
We have $T_i=Q_i\succeq q_i I$ where $q_i>0$ or $T_i=\alpha A_i\tr A_i-\epsilon_i I$.
We let $\bar\tau =\min\{ \max \{ q_i,\lambda_{++}^{\alpha A_i\tr A_i-\epsilon_i I} \} : i=1,\dots, p\}$
and $\bar D=D-2\epsilon_0(c_3+c_4)I$. For 
$\sigma=\min\{\lambda_{\min}(\bar D), \bar\tau,\frac{\epsilon_0-1}{\alpha\beta}\}>0$
we arrive at the inequality (\ref{Lbarmon}), showing monotonicity of $\{\bar {\mathcal L_k}\}_{k\ge 1}$.
%

{\bf (ii)}  If $\{{\bf x}^k, y^k, z^k\}_{k\ge 0}$ is a bounded  sequence,
then 
$\|B\tr\Delta z^k\|^2+
\|\Delta y^k\|^2$ is also bounded, and bounded from below by zero.
Hence we only need to show that 
$\mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k)$ is bounded. 
By the boundedness of $\{({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k)\}_{k\ge 0}$,
the terms  $\langle z^k, {\bf Ax}^k+By^k+b\rangle$ and $\|{\bf Ax}^k+By^k+b\|^2$
are bounded. By A1 the function $f_i, i=1,\dots,p$ are coercive,
since $\{{\bf x}^k\}_{k\ge 0}$ is bounded, then $\{f_i(x_i^k)\}_{k\ge 0}$ is bounded for $i=1,\dots,p$. 
By A2, the function $h$ is bounded from below.
Thus, $\{\mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k)\}_{k\ge 0}$
is bounded from below.
%
Since $\{\bar{\mathcal L}_k\}_{k\ge 1}$ is bounded from below and by part (i) it is 
monotonically decreasing then we conclude that $\{\bar{\mathcal L}_k\}_{k\ge 1}$ it converges.  $\square$

\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{samelimit}
Suppose that A1-A4 hold and   $({\bf x}^*,y^*,z^*)\in\omega(\{ ({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k)\}_{k\ge 0})$,
then
\[
\bar{\mathcal L}({\bf x}^*,y^*,z^*, y^*,z^*)
=
\mathcal L^{\alpha} ({\bf x}^*,y^*,z^*) 
=
\sum_{i=1}^p f_i(x_i^*)+h(y^*).
\]

\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let $({\bf x}^*,y^*,z^*)\in\omega(\{ ({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k)\}_{k\ge 0})$
and let the subsequence $\{({\bf x}^{k_j},y^{k_j},z^{k_j})\}_{j\ge 0}$ of the 
PADMM algorithm converges to 
$({\bf x}^*,y^*,z^*)$.
Clearly $\|\Delta y^{k_j}\|$ and $\|B\tr \Delta z^{k_j}\|$ both converge to zero as $j$ goes to infinity.
This, together with Lemma
 Lemma \ref{thm-cluster} and \ref{thm-cluster0} give
%
\begin{eqnarray*}
\lim_{j\to\infty} \bar {\mathcal L}_{k_j} =\lim_{j\to\infty} \mathcal L^{\alpha} (x^{k_j},y^{k_j},z^{k_j})
&=&\mathcal L^{\alpha}(x^*,y^*,z^*)\\
&=&\sum_{i=1}^pf_i(x_i^*)+h(y^*)
=\bar{\mathcal L}({\bf x}^*,y^*,z^*, y^*,z^*). \quad\quad\square
\end{eqnarray*}
%
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{lma-D}
{(subgradient bound for $\bar{\mathcal L}_k$)}
Let $\{({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k)\}_{k\ge 0}$ be a sequence generated by the PADMM algorithm
and assume that $\big(\{d_{x_i}^k\}_{i=1}^p,d_y^k,d_z^k\big)\in\partial \mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k)$. Then 
%
\[
s^{k}:=\Big( \{s^{k}_{x_i}\}_{i=1}^p, s^{k}_y, s^{k}_z, s^{k}_{y'},s^{k}_{z'} \Big)\in
\partial \bar{\mathcal L}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k},y^{k-1},z^{k-1}),\quad k\ge 1
\]
%
where
%
$s_{x_i}^{k}:=d^{k}_{x_i}, i=1,\dots, p$,
$s_y^{k}:=d^{k}_y+2\epsilon_0c_3 \Delta y^{k}$,
$s_z^{k}:=d^{k}_z+2\epsilon_0c_5BB\tr \Delta z^{k}$,
$s_{y'}^{k}:=-2\epsilon_0c_3 \Delta y^{k}$,
$s_{z'}^{k}:=-2\epsilon_0c_5BB\tr \Delta z^{k}$,
and $\epsilon_0>1$, and $c_3$ and $c_5$ are defined in  (\ref{quantities}).
Moreover,
\begin{eqnarray}\label{nD}
|||s^{k}|||\le \tilde\rho \Big(\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k}\|+\|\Delta y^{k}\|+\|\Delta z^{k}\|\Big),
\end{eqnarray}
where 
$
\tilde\rho:=\max\Big\{
\|{\bf Q}\|+\|{\bf A}\|^2,\;
\|P\|+\alpha \|{\bf A}\|\|B\|+4\epsilon_0c_3, \;
\|{\bf A}\|  +\|B\|+4\epsilon_0c_5\|B\|^2 + \frac{1}{\alpha\beta}\Big\},
$
and $\|{\bf Q}$ and $\|{\bf A}\|$ are defined in Lemma \ref{thm-d}.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let $k\ge 1$ be fixed and $(\{d_{x_i}^{k}\}_{i=1}^p, d_y^{k}, d_z^{k})\in \partial \mathcal L^{\alpha}(x^k,y^k,z^k)$. By taking partial derivatives of $\bar{\mathcal L}$ with respect to $x,y,z,y',z'$ and evaluating 
them at $({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k,y^{k-1},z^{k-1})$ we obtain
%
\begin{eqnarray*}
%s_{x_i}^{k}&:=& 
\partial_{x_i} \bar{\mathcal L}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k},y^{k-1},z^{k-1})
&=&\partial_{x_i} \mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k})
\ni d_{x_i}^{k},\; i=1,\dots,p;\\
%s_y^{k}&:=&
\nabla_y  \bar{\mathcal L} ({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k},y^{k-1},z^{k-1})
&=&\nabla_y \mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k})
+2\epsilon_0c_3 \Delta y^k=
d_y^{k}+2\epsilon_0c_3 \Delta y^k;\\
%s_z^{k}&:=&
\nabla_z  \bar{\mathcal L}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k},y^{k-1},z^{k-1})
&=&\nabla_z \mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k})
+2\epsilon_0c_5 BB\tr \Delta z^{k}=
d_z^{k}
+2\epsilon_0c_5 BB\tr\Delta z^{k};\\
%s_{y'}^{k}&:=&
\nabla_{y'}  \bar{\mathcal L}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k},y^{k-1},z^{k-1})
&=&-2\epsilon_0c_3\Delta y^k;\\
%d_{z'}^{k}&:=&
\nabla_{z'}  \bar{\mathcal L}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k},y^{k-1},z^{k-1})
&=&-2\epsilon_0c_5BB\tr \Delta z^k.
\end{eqnarray*}
%
These equations follow that 
\begin{eqnarray*}
s^k =
\left[
\begin{array}{c}
s^k_{x_1}\\
\vdots\\
s^k_{x_p}\\
s^k_{y} \\ 
s^k_{z}\\
s^k_{y'}\\
s^k_{z'}
\end{array}
\right]
=
\left[
\begin{array}{l}
d^k_{x_1}\\
\vdots\\[.1in]
d^k_{x_p}\\
d_y^{k}+2\epsilon_0c_3 \Delta y^k \\ 
d_z^{k}+2\epsilon_0c_5 BB\tr\Delta z^{k}\\
-2\epsilon_0c_3\Delta y^k\\
-2\epsilon_0c_5BB\tr \Delta z^k
\end{array}
\right]\in \partial \bar{\mathcal L}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k},y^{k-1},z^{k-1}).
\end{eqnarray*} 
%
By the triangle inequality we have
%
\begin{eqnarray*}
&\|s_y^{k}\|\le \|d^{k}_y\|+2\epsilon_0c_3\|\Delta y^k\|,\quad\quad
\|s_z^{k}\|\le\|d^{k}_z\|+2\epsilon_0c_5\|B\|^2 \|\Delta z^k\|,&\\
&\|s_{y'}^{k}\|\le 2\epsilon_0c_3\|\Delta y^k\|,\quad\quad
\|s_z^{k}\|\le 2\epsilon_0c_5 \|B\|^2 \|\Delta z^k\|.&
\end{eqnarray*}
%
Thus
\begin{eqnarray*}
|||s^{k}|||&\le&  \sum_{i=1}^p\|s_{x_i}^{k}\|+\|s_y^{k}\|+\|s_z^{k}\|+ \|s_{y'}^{k}\|+\|s_z^{k}\|\\
&\le& \sum_{i=1}^p \|d^{k}_{x_i}\|+  \|d^{k}_y\|+\|d^{k}_z\|+
4\epsilon_0c_3\|\Delta y^{k}\|+
4\epsilon_0c_5 \|B\|^2 \|\Delta z^k\|.
\end{eqnarray*}
%
By Lemma \ref{thm-d}, we have 
%
\begin{eqnarray*}
&|||s^{k}|||\le
\Big(\|{\bf Q}\|+\|{\bf A}\|^2\Big) \sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k}\|
+\Big(\|P\|+\alpha \|{\bf A}\|\|B\| +4\epsilon_0c_3 \Big)      \|\Delta y^{k}\|&\\
&+\Big(\|{\bf A}\|  +\|B\|+4\epsilon_0c_5\|B\|^2+\frac{1}{\alpha\beta}\Big)  \|\Delta z^{k}\|
\le \tilde\rho \Big( \sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k}\|+   \|\Delta y^{k}\|+  \|\Delta z^{k}\|\Big). \quad \square&
\end{eqnarray*}

\end{proof}

\begin{lemma} \label{bddseq0}
Suppose that A1-A4 hold and $\sigma$ defined in Lemma \ref{thm1} is positive.
Then the sequence 
$\{{\bf x}^k, y^k, z^k\}_{k\ge 0}$ generated by the PADMM algorithm (\ref{padmm}) is bounded,
and $
\lim_{k\to \infty} \|\Delta x_1^{k}\|=\dots=\lim_{k\to \infty} \|\Delta x_p^{k}\|=
\lim_{k\to \infty} \|\Delta y^{k}\|=\lim_{k\to \infty} \|\Delta z^{k}\|=0.
$
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let $\{({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k)\}_{k\ge 0}$ be a sequence generated by the PADMM algorithm.
%
By $\sigma>0$, the sequence $\{\bar{\mathcal L}_k\}_{k\ge 1}$ 
defined in (\ref{Lbark}) is monotonically decreasing, hence it is upper bounded by 
$\bar{\mathcal L}_1=\bar{\mathcal L}({\bf x}^1,y^1,z^1,y^0,z^0)$.
This follows that 
%
\begin{eqnarray}\label{ineq10}
\begin{array}{c}
\sum_{i=1}^pf(x_i^{k})+h(y^{k})
+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|{\bf Ax}^{k}+By^{k}
+\alpha^{-1}z^{k}+b\|^2-\frac{1}{2\alpha}\|z^{k}\|^2
\\[.1in]
+\sigma \sum_{i=1}^p \|\Delta x_i^{k}\|^2
 +\sigma\|\Delta z^{k}\|^2
+(\sigma+\epsilon_0c_3) \|\Delta y^{k}\|^2
+\epsilon_0c_5\|B\tr \Delta z^{k}\|^2
\le \bar{\mathcal L}_1
 \end{array}
\end{eqnarray}
%
for all $k\in\mathbb Z_+$.
By Lemma \ref{bounddual} (iii), (\ref{ineq10}) leads to 
%
\begin{eqnarray}\label{thmbdd-eq1}
\begin{array}{c}
\sum_{i=1}^pf(x_i^{k})+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|{\bf Ax}^{k}+By^{k}+\alpha^{-1}z^{k}+b\|^2
+r_1\|\Delta y^{k}\|^2\\[.1in]
+ \sigma\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x^{k}\|^2
+ r_2\|B\tr \Delta z^{k}\|^2
+\sigma\|\Delta z^{k}\|^2
\le\bar{\mathcal L}_1
%- \inf_{x,y}\Big\{g(x)- c_1 \Big\|\nabla g(x)\Big\|^2\Big\}
-\inf_y\Big\{ h(y)-c_1 \|\nabla h(y)\|^2 \Big\},
\end{array}
\end{eqnarray}
%
where $r_1:= \epsilon_0c_3+\sigma-\|P\|^2c_1>0$
and $r_2:=\epsilon_0c_5-c_6>0$. 
By A2,  since $h$ is $L_h$ Lipschitz differentiable then for any $k\ge 1$ 
and $\delta>0$ we have
%
$
h\big(y^k-\delta \nabla h(y^k)\big)\le h(y^k)- 
\big(\delta-\frac{L_h\delta^2}{2}\big)\|\nabla h(y^k)\|^2.
$
%
Again by A2, $h$ is bounded from below then
%
\begin{eqnarray}\label{hbd}
-\infty<\inf\{h(y)- \Big(\delta-\frac{L_h\delta^2}{2}\Big)\|\nabla h(y)\|^2: \; y\in\mathbb R^q\}.
\end{eqnarray}
%
We choose $\delta (>0)$ such that 
$\delta-\frac{L_h\delta^2}{2}=c_1$. By (\ref{hbd}), the right hand side of (\ref{thmbdd-eq1}) is finite
hence
%
\begin{eqnarray}\label{finite}
\sum_{i=1}^pf(x_i^{k})+\|{\bf Ax}^{k}+By^{k}+\alpha^{-1}z^{k}+b\|^2
+\|\Delta y^{k}\|^2 +\|\Delta z^k\|^2<+\infty.
\end{eqnarray}
%
By A1, since $f_i, i=1,\dots,p$ are coercive and $\sum_{i=1}^pf(x_i^{k})<+\infty$, then the sequence 
$\{x_i^k\}_{k\ge 0}$  is bounded for $i=1,\dots,p$, and so are 
$\{{\bf x}^k\}_{k\ge 0}$ and $\{{\bf Ax}^k\}_{k\ge 0}$.
%
%In addition, by (\ref{finite}) the sequences 
%$\{Ax^{k}+By^{k}+\alpha^{-1}z^{k}+c\}_{k\ge k_0}$ and $\{ \Delta y^{k}\}_{k\ge k_0}$ are bounded, 
%then $\{A\Delta x^k\}_{k\ge k_0}$ and $\{B\Delta y^k\}_{k\ge k_0}$
%are bounded which follows that $\{\Delta z^k\}_{k\ge 0}$ is bounded.

By the $z$ iterate of PADMM we have
$
By^{k} = \frac{1}{\alpha\beta} \Delta z^{k} -{\bf Ax}^{k}-b.
$
By (\ref{finite}), $\{\Delta z^k\}_{k\ge 0}$ is bounded.
By A3, $B\tr B$ is invertible, thus $\{y^k\}_{k\ge 0}$ is bounded.
Finally, by (\ref{finite}) $\{{\bf Ax}^{k}+By^{k}+\frac{1}{\alpha}z^{k}\}_{k\ge 0}$ is bounded
and ${\bf Ax}^k$ and $By^k$ are bounded, so 
$\{z^k\}_{k\ge 0}$ is then bounded.
%
Summing up (\ref{Lbarmon}) for $k=1,\dots, K-1$, $K\ge 2$ gives
%
\[
\sum_{k=1}^{K}
\Big\{\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k}\|^2
+\|\Delta y^{k}\|^2
+\|\Delta z^{k}\|^2\Big\}\le \frac{1}{\sigma}(\bar{\mathcal L}_1 - \bar{\mathcal L}_K) .
\]
Since $\{({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k)\}_{k\ge 0}$ is bounded, by Lemma \ref{thm1} (ii) the right hand side is finite for any $K$.
We let $K$ approach to infinity to obtain 
\begin{eqnarray*}
\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}
\Big\{\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k}\|^2 +\|\Delta y^{k}\|^2+\|\Delta z^{k}\|^2\Big\}<
\frac{1}{\sigma}(\bar{\mathcal L}_1 - \inf_{k\ge 1}\bar{\mathcal L}_k) <
+\infty.
\end{eqnarray*}
This follows 
$
\displaystyle{\lim_{k\to \infty}} \Big(\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k}\|^2 +\|\Delta y^{k}\|^2+\|\Delta z^{k}\|^2\Big)=0,
$

\alpha B\tr ({\bf Ax}^{k}+By^{k}+b)+B\tr z^{k-1}-w^k=0
\]
which together with the $z$-iterate ${\bf Ax}^{k}+By^{k}+b=\frac{1}{\alpha\beta}(z^k-z^{k-1})$ we obtain the result.


{\bf (ii)} By A3 and the $z$ iterate of the PADMM algorithm we have $\Delta z^{k+1}\in {\rm Im}(B)$, thus 
 $\lambda_{++}^{B\tr B}\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|^2\le \|B\tr \Delta z^{k+1}\|^2$.
Part (i) follows 
$B\tr \Delta z^{k+1}=\beta\Delta w^{k+1}+(1-\beta) B\tr \Delta z^{k}$ and 
equivalently 
%
\begin{eqnarray*}
B\tr \Delta z^{k+1}=\rho(\beta)
\Big(\frac{\beta\Delta w^{k+1}}{\rho(\beta)} \Big)
+|1-\beta| \Big({\rm sign}(1-\beta) B\tr \Delta z^k\Big),
\end{eqnarray*}
where ${\rm sign} (\lambda)=1$ if $\lambda\ge 0$ and ${\rm sign} (\lambda)=-1$ if $\lambda<0$.
By $\rho(\beta)+|1-\beta|=1$ and the convexity of $\|\cdot\|^2$ 
we have
%
\begin{eqnarray}\label{gg}
\|B\tr \Delta z^{k+1}\|^2
\le  \frac{\beta^2}{\rho(\beta)}  \|\Delta w^{k+1}\|^2
+|1-\beta| \|B\tr \Delta z^{k}\|^2.%-|1-\beta| \Big\| B^*\Delta z^{k+1}\Big\|^2.
\end{eqnarray}
This also follows that 
%
\begin{eqnarray*}\label{gg}
\rho(\beta)\lambda_{++}^{B\tr B} \|\Delta z^{k+1}\|^2&\le& \rho(\beta)\|B\tr \Delta z^{k+1}\|^2\\
%
&\le&  \frac{\beta^2}{\rho(\beta)}  \|\Delta w^{k+1}\|^2
+|1-\beta| \|B\tr \Delta z^{k}\|^2-|1-\beta| \| B\tr \Delta z^{k+1}\|^2.
\end{eqnarray*}
%
Rearrange this to obtain
%
\begin{eqnarray}\label{gg}
\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|^2\le
 \frac{\beta^2}{\rho(\beta)^2\lambda_{++}^{B\tr B} }  \|\Delta w^{k+1}\|^2
+\frac{|1-\beta|}{\rho(\beta)\lambda_{++}^{B\tr B} } \|B\tr \Delta z^{k}\|^2
-\frac{|1-\beta|}{\rho(\beta)\lambda_{++}^{B\tr B} } \| B\tr \Delta z^{k+1}\|^2.
\end{eqnarray}
%
By the optimality condition of $y$ subproblem we have 
\[
\Delta w^{k+1}=-P\Delta y^{k+1}+P\Delta y^k+\nabla h(y^{k})-\nabla h(y^{k+1}).
\]
By $\|a+b\|^2\le 2\|a\|^2+2\|b\|^2$ and the fact that $\nabla h$ has $L_h$ Lipschitz gradients
we obtain
\[
\|\Delta w^{k+1}\|^2\le 2(\|P\|+L_h)^2\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|^2+2\|P\|^2 \|\Delta y^k\|^2.
\]
Exploit this in (\ref{gg}) to get
\begin{eqnarray*}\label{gg0}
\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|^2&\le&
 \frac{2\beta^2 (\|P\|+L_h)^2}{\rho(\beta)^2\lambda_{++}^{B\tr B} }          \|\Delta y^{k+1}\|^2
 + \frac{2\beta^2\|P\|^2}{\rho(\beta)^2\lambda_{++}^{B\tr B} }    \|\Delta y^k\|^2\\
 &&+\frac{|1-\beta|}{\rho(\beta)\lambda_{++}^{B\tr B} } \|B\tr \Delta z^{k}\|^2
-\frac{|1-\beta|}{\rho(\beta)\lambda_{++}^{B\tr B} } \| B\tr \Delta z^{k+1}\|^2.
\end{eqnarray*}
We divide both sides by $\alpha\beta$ to get 
%
\begin{eqnarray*}
\frac{1}{\alpha\beta}\Big\|\Delta z^{k+1}\Big\|^2
\le c_4 \Big\|\Delta y^{k+1}\Big\|^2
+c_3 \|\Delta y^{k}\|^2+c_5 \Big\|B\tr \Delta z^{k}\Big\|^2
-c_5 \Big\| B\tr \Delta z^{k+1}\Big\|^2.
\end{eqnarray*}

{\bf (iii).} By part (i) we have
%
$\beta B\tr z^{k+1}=\beta w^{k+1}+(1-\beta) B\tr (z^k-z^{k+1})$ 
which can be written equivalently as follows
%
\begin{eqnarray*}
\beta B\tr z^{k+1}= \rho(\beta)\cdot \frac{\beta w^{k+1}}{\rho(\beta)}
+|1-\beta|\cdot {\rm sign}(1-\beta) B\tr (z^k-z^{k+1}).
\end{eqnarray*}
By $\rho(\beta)+|1-\beta|=1$ and the convexity of $\|\cdot\|^2$
we get
%
\begin{eqnarray*}
\beta^2\lambda_{++}^{B\tr B} \|z^{k+1}\|^2
\le   \beta^2 \|B\tr z^{k+1}\|^2
\le
\rho(\beta)\cdot \Big\| \frac{\beta w^{k+1}}{\rho(\beta)}\Big\|^2
+|1-\beta| \|B\tr \Delta z^{k+1}\|^2.
\end{eqnarray*}
%
Simplify and rearrange to get
%
\begin{eqnarray*}
\|z^{k+1}\|^2
\le 
\frac{1}{\rho(\beta)\lambda_{++}^{B\tr B}}      \|w^{k+1}\|^2
+\frac{|1-\beta|}{\beta^2 \lambda_{++}^{B\tr B}      } \|B\tr \Delta z^{k+1}\|^2.
\end{eqnarray*}
%
Exploit $\|w^{k+1}\|^2\le 2 \|P\|^2 \|\Delta y^{k+1}\|^2+2\|\nabla h(y^{k+1})\|^2$
to obtain 
%
\begin{eqnarray*}
\|z^{k+1}\|^2
\le
\frac{2\|P\|^2}{\rho(\beta)\lambda_{++}^{B\tr B}}  \|\Delta y^{k+1}\|^2
+ \frac{2}{\rho(\beta)\lambda_{++}^{B\tr B}} \|\nabla h(y^{k+1})\|^2
+\frac{|1-\beta|}{\beta^2\lambda_{++}^{B\tr B}} \|B\tr \Delta z^{k+1}\|^2.
\end{eqnarray*}
%
Divide both sides by $2\alpha$ to obtain the result.
This concludes the proof.  $\square$
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{chgL}
{(change of $\mathcal L^{\alpha}$ during each variable update)} 
Suppose that A1-A4 hold. The iterates in PADMM algorithm (\ref{padmm}) satisfy
%
\begin{itemize}
\item [(i)] $\mathcal L^{\alpha}(x_{<i}^{k+1},x_i^k, x^{k}_{>i},y^k,z^k)-
\mathcal L^{\alpha}(x_{<i}^{k+1},x_i^{k+1}, x^{k}_{>i},y^k,z^k)\ge \frac{1}{2} \|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|_{T_i}^2$ where
$T_i=Q_i$ or $T_i=\alpha A_i\tr A_i-\epsilon_i I$ where $\epsilon_i >0$ defined in A4 for $i=1,\dots, p$.
%
\item [(ii)]
$\mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^{k+1},y^k, z^k)-\mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^{k+1},y^{k+1},z^{k})
\ge \frac{1}{2} \|\Delta y^{k+1}\|_D^2$, where $D$ is defined in (\ref{quantities}).
\item [(iii)] $\mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^{k+1},y^{k+1}, z^k)-
\mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^{k+1},y^{k+1},z^{k+1})=-\frac{1}{\alpha\beta}\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|^2.$
%
\end{itemize}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
{\bf (i)} Let $k\in\mathbb Z_+$ and $i\in\{1,\dots,p\}$ be fixed.
By the $x_i$ subproblem we have
\[
\mathcal L^{\alpha}(x_{<i}^{k+1},x_i^{k}, x^{k}_{>i},y^k,z^k)-
\mathcal L^{\alpha}(x_{<i}^{k+1},x_i^{k+1}, x^{k}_{>i},y^k,z^k)
\ge \|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|_{Q_i}^2.
\]
%
On the other hand, by the optimality condition of $x_i$-sub-minimization problem we have 
$ \bar{d_i}\in\partial f_i(x_i^{k+1})$
where 
\[
\bar{d_i}:=-A_i \tr z^k-
\alpha A_i\tr \big(A_{<i} x_{<i}^{k+1}+A_ix_i^{k+1}+A_{>i}x_{>i}^k+By^k+b
\big).
\]
By this we then have
\begin{eqnarray*}
&\mathcal L^{\alpha}(x_{<i}^{k+1},x_i^k, x^{k}_{>i},y^k,z^k)-
\mathcal L^{\alpha}(x_{<i}^{k+1},x_i^{k+1}, x^{k}_{>i},y^k,z^k)& \\[.1in]
&=f_i(x_i^k)-f_i(x_i^{k+1})
+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|A_i\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|^2-\langle \bar{d_i}, \Delta x_i^{k+1}\rangle&
\\[.1in]
&\ge \frac{\alpha}{2}\|A_i\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|^2
- \frac{\epsilon_i}{2}\|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|^2
=\frac 12 \|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|_{\alpha A_i\tr A_i-\epsilon_iI}^2.&
\end{eqnarray*}

%%%%
{\bf (ii)}
Let $k\ge 0$ be fixed. From the optimality condition of $y$ minimization problem 
we have
\begin{eqnarray*}
\nabla h(y^{k+1})+\alpha B\tr ({\bf Ax}^{k+1}+By^{k+1}+b)
+B\tr z^k+P \Delta y^{k+1}=0.
\end{eqnarray*}
Multiply this equation by $\Delta y^{k+1}$ and rearrange to obtain
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:2}
- \alpha\big\langle B\tr ({\bf Ax}^{k+1}+ By^{k+1}+b),\Delta y^{k+1}\big\rangle 
-\langle B\tr z^k, \Delta y^{k+1}\rangle
=\langle \nabla h(y^{k+1}),\Delta y^{k+1}\rangle +\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|_P^2.
\end{eqnarray}
By this and the fact that $h(y)$ is $L_h$ Lipschitz continuous we then get 
%
\begin{eqnarray*}
&\mathcal L^{\alpha}(x^{k+1},y^k,z^k)-\mathcal L^{\alpha}(x^{k+1},y^{k+1},z^{k})&
\\[.1in]
&= h(y^k)-h(y^{k+1})
+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|{\bf Ax}^{k+1}+By^k+b\|^2
-\frac{\alpha}{2}\|{\bf Ax}^{k+1}+By^{k+1}+b\|^2
-\langle B\tr z^k, \Delta y^{k+1} \rangle&
\\[.1in]
 &=h(y^k)-h(y^{k+1})
+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|B\Delta y^{k+1}\|^2
-\alpha \langle \Delta y^{k+1}, B\tr ({\bf Ax}^{k+1}+By^{k+1}+b)\rangle 
-\langle B\tr z^k, \Delta y^{k+1} \rangle&
\\[.1in]
&=h(y^k)-h(y^{k+1})
+\langle \nabla h(y^{k+1}),\Delta y^{k+1}\rangle +\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|_P^2
+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|B\Delta y^{k+1}\|^2
&\\[.1in]
&\ge\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|_P^2
+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|B\Delta y^{k+1}\|^2
-\frac{L_h}{2}\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|^2 = 
\frac{1}{2} \|\Delta y^{k+1}\|_{D}^2.&
\end{eqnarray*}
%
%
{\bf (iii)} By the $z$ iterate of the algorithm we obtain
\begin{eqnarray*}
&\mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^{k+1},y^{k+1}, z^k)-
\mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^{k+1},y^{k+1},z^{k+1})=
\langle z^k-z^{k+1}, {\bf Ax}^{k+1}+By^{k+1}+b\rangle
=-\frac{1}{\alpha\beta}\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|^2.&
\end{eqnarray*}
%
That completes the proof. $\square$
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}
By Lemma \ref{chgL} we have 
\begin{eqnarray*}
&\mathcal L^{\alpha}(x^{k+1},y^{k+1},z^{k+1})=\mathcal L^{\alpha}(x^{k+1},y^{k+1},z^{k}) 
+ \frac{1}{\alpha\beta}\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|^2
&\\[.1in]&
\le  \mathcal L^{\alpha}(x^{k+1},y^{k},z^{k}) + \frac{1}{\alpha\beta}\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|^2
-\frac{1}{2} \|\Delta y^{k+1}\|_{D}^2 
&\\[.1in]&
\le \mathcal L^{\alpha}(x^{k},y^{k},z^{k})
+ \frac{1}{\alpha\beta}\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|^2
-\frac{1}{2} \|\Delta y^{k+1}\|_{D}^2 -\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^p \|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|^2_{T_i}.&
\end{eqnarray*}
By Lemma \ref{bounddual} for $\epsilon_0>1$ we have 
\[
\frac{\epsilon_0}{\alpha\beta}\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|^2
\le\epsilon_0c_4 \|\Delta y^{k+1}\|^2
+\epsilon_0c_3 \|\Delta y^{k}\|^2+
\epsilon_0c_5 \|B\tr \Delta z^{k}\|^2
-\epsilon_0c_5\| B\tr \Delta z^{k+1}\|^2.
\]
Add this to the latter inequality and rearrange to obtain (\ref{chgLiter}). $\square$
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{thm1}
%{\bf (monotonicity/convergence of $\bar{\mathcal L}$)}
Suppose that A1-A4 hold, and 
\[
\bar\tau =\min\{ \max \{ q_i,\lambda_{++}^{\alpha A_i\tr A_i-\epsilon_i I} \} : i=1,\dots, p\}.
\]
 If $\sigma=\min\{\lambda_{\min}(\bar D), \bar\tau,\frac{\epsilon_0-1}{\alpha\beta}\}>0$ where 
 $\bar D$ is defined in (\ref{quantities}), then
the following assertions hold.
%
\begin{itemize}
\item [(i)] The sequence $\{\bar {\mathcal L_k}\}_{k\ge 1}$ is monotonically decreasing and 
%
\begin{eqnarray}\label{Lbarmon}
\bar{\mathcal L}_{k+1}+\sigma
\big[\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|^2
+ \|\Delta y^{k+1}\|^2+
\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|^2\big]
\le \bar{\mathcal L}_k.
\end{eqnarray}
%
%
\item [(ii)] If the sequence $\{{\bf x}^k, y^k, z^k\}_{k\ge 0}$ generated by the PADMM is bounded 
then $\bar{\mathcal L}_k$ is bounded from below for all $k \in \mathbb N$  and converges as $k$ approaches infinity.
%%
%\item [(iii)] If $B\tr B$ is invertible, then $\{{\bf x}^k, y^k, z^k\}_{k\ge 0}$ is bounded.
%\item [(iv)]  If $\{{\bf x}^k, y^k, z^k\}_{k\ge 0}$ is bounded
%then 
%$\lim_{k\to \infty} \|\Delta x_i^{k}\|=\lim_{k\to \infty} \|\Delta y^{k}\|=\lim_{k\to \infty} \|\Delta z^{k}\|=0.$
\end{itemize}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
{\bf (i)} By (\ref{chgLiter}) and (\ref{Lbark}) we obtain 
\[
\bar{\mathcal L}_{k+1}
+\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^p \|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|^2_{T_i}
+\frac 12\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|^2_{D-2\epsilon_0(c_3+c_4)}+
\displaystyle{\frac{\epsilon_0-1}{\alpha\beta}}\big\|\Delta z^{k+1}\big\|^2
\le \bar{\mathcal L}_k.
\]
We have $T_i=Q_i\succeq q_i I$ where $q_i>0$ or $T_i=\alpha A_i\tr A_i-\epsilon_i I$.
We let $\bar\tau =\min\{ \max \{ q_i,\lambda_{++}^{\alpha A_i\tr A_i-\epsilon_i I} \} : i=1,\dots, p\}$
and $\bar D=D-2\epsilon_0(c_3+c_4)I$. For 
$\sigma=\min\{\lambda_{\min}(\bar D), \bar\tau,\frac{\epsilon_0-1}{\alpha\beta}\}>0$
we arrive at the inequality (\ref{Lbarmon}), showing monotonicity of $\{\bar {\mathcal L_k}\}_{k\ge 1}$.
%

{\bf (ii)}  If $\{{\bf x}^k, y^k, z^k\}_{k\ge 0}$ is a bounded  sequence,
then 
$\|B\tr\Delta z^k\|^2+
\|\Delta y^k\|^2$ is also bounded, and bounded from below by zero.
Hence we only need to show that 
$\mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k)$ is bounded. 
By the boundedness of $\{({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k)\}_{k\ge 0}$,
the terms  $\langle z^k, {\bf Ax}^k+By^k+b\rangle$ and $\|{\bf Ax}^k+By^k+b\|^2$
are bounded. By A1 the function $f_i, i=1,\dots,p$ are coercive,
since $\{{\bf x}^k\}_{k\ge 0}$ is bounded, then $\{f_i(x_i^k)\}_{k\ge 0}$ is bounded for $i=1,\dots,p$. 
By A2, the function $h$ is bounded from below.
Thus, $\{\mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k)\}_{k\ge 0}$
is bounded from below.
%
Since $\{\bar{\mathcal L}_k\}_{k\ge 1}$ is bounded from below and by part (i) it is 
monotonically decreasing then we conclude that $\{\bar{\mathcal L}_k\}_{k\ge 1}$ it converges.  $\square$

\end{proof}

=

=

 Lemma \ref{thm-cluster} and \ref{thm-cluster0} give

Let $\{({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k)\}_{k\ge 0}$ be a sequence generated by the PADMM algorithm
and assume that $\big(\{d_{x_i}^k\}_{i=1}^p,d_y^k,d_z^k\big)\in\partial \mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k)$. Then 
%
\[

\partial \bar{\mathcal L}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k},y^{k-1},z^{k-1}),\quad k\ge 1
\]
%
where
%
$s_{x_i}^{k}:=d^{k}_{x_i}, i=1,\dots, p$,
$s_y^{k}:=d^{k}_y+2\epsilon_0c_3 \Delta y^{k}$,

\begin{eqnarray}\label{nD}
|||s^{k}|||\le \tilde\rho \Big(\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k}\|+\|\Delta y^{k}\|+\|\Delta z^{k}\|\Big),

$
\tilde\rho:=\max\Big\{
\|{\bf Q}\|+\|{\bf A}\|^2,\;
\|P\|+\alpha \|{\bf A}\|\|B\|+4\epsilon_0c_3, \;
\|{\bf A}\|  +\|B\|+4\epsilon_0c_5\|B\|^2 + \frac{1}{\alpha\beta}\Big\},

\begin{proof}
Let $k\ge 1$ be fixed and $(\{d_{x_i}^{k}\}_{i=1}^p, d_y^{k}, d_z^{k})\in \partial \mathcal L^{\alpha}(x^k,y^k,z^k)$. By taking partial derivatives of $\bar{\mathcal L}$ with respect to $x,y,z,y',z'$ and evaluating

%
\begin{eqnarray*}
%s_{x_i}^{k}&:=& 
\partial_{x_i} \bar{\mathcal L}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k},y^{k-1},z^{k-1})
&=&\partial_{x_i} \mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k})
\ni d_{x_i}^{k},\; i=1,\dots,p;\\
%s_y^{k}&:=&
\nabla_y  \bar{\mathcal L} ({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k},y^{k-1},z^{k-1})
&=&\nabla_y \mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k})
+2\epsilon_0c_3 \Delta y^k=
d_y^{k}+2\epsilon_0c_3 \Delta y^k;\\
%s_z^{k}&:=&
\nabla_z  \bar{\mathcal L}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k},y^{k-1},z^{k-1})
&=&\nabla_z \mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k})
+2\epsilon_0c_5 BB\tr \Delta z^{k}=
d_z^{k}
+2\epsilon_0c_5 BB\tr\Delta z^{k};\\
%s_{y'}^{k}&:=&
\nabla_{y'}  \bar{\mathcal L}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k},y^{k-1},z^{k-1})
&=&-2\epsilon_0c_3\Delta y^k;\\
%d_{z'}^{k}&:=&
\nabla_{z'}  \bar{\mathcal L}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k},y^{k-1},z^{k-1})
&=&-2\epsilon_0c_5BB\tr \Delta z^k.
\end{eqnarray*}
%
These equations follow that 
\begin{eqnarray*}
s^k =
\left[
\begin{array}{c}
s^k_{x_1}\\
\vdots\\
s^k_{x_p}\\
s^k_{y} \\ 
s^k_{z}\\
s^k_{y'}\\
s^k_{z'}

=

d_y^{k}+2\epsilon_0c_3 \Delta y^k \\

%

\|s_z^{k}\|\le\|d^{k}_z\|+2\epsilon_0c_5\|B\|^2 \|\Delta z^k\|,&\\

Thus

|||s^{k}|||&\le&  \sum_{i=1}^p\|s_{x_i}^{k}\|+\|s_y^{k}\|+\|s_z^{k}\|+ \|s_{y'}^{k}\|+\|s_z^{k}\|\\

\end{proof}

\begin{lemma} \label{bddseq0}
Suppose that A1-A4 hold and $\sigma$ defined in Lemma \ref{thm1} is positive.
Then the sequence 
$\{{\bf x}^k, y^k, z^k\}_{k\ge 0}$ generated by the PADMM algorithm (\ref{padmm}) is bounded,

Let $\{({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k)\}_{k\ge 0}$ be a sequence generated by the PADMM algorithm.

defined in (\ref{Lbark}) is monotonically decreasing, hence it is upper bounded by 
$\bar{\mathcal L}_1=\bar{\mathcal L}({\bf x}^1,y^1,z^1,y^0,z^0)$.
This follows that

\begin{eqnarray}\label{ineq10}
\begin{array}{c}

+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|{\bf Ax}^{k}+By^{k}
+\alpha^{-1}z^{k}+b\|^2-\frac{1}{2\alpha}\|z^{k}\|^2
\\[.1in]
+\sigma \sum_{i=1}^p \|\Delta x_i^{k}\|^2
 +\sigma\|\Delta z^{k}\|^2
+(\sigma+\epsilon_0c_3) \|\Delta y^{k}\|^2

\le \bar{\mathcal L}_1
 \end{array}
\end{eqnarray}
%
for all $k\in\mathbb Z_+$.
By Lemma \ref{bounddual} (iii), (\ref{ineq10}) leads to 
%
\begin{eqnarray}\label{thmbdd-eq1}
\begin{array}{c}
\sum_{i=1}^pf(x_i^{k})+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|{\bf Ax}^{k}+By^{k}+\alpha^{-1}z^{k}+b\|^2
+r_1\|\Delta y^{k}\|^2\\[.1in]
+ \sigma\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x^{k}\|^2
+ r_2\|B\tr \Delta z^{k}\|^2
+\sigma\|\Delta z^{k}\|^2
\le\bar{\mathcal L}_1
%- \inf_{x,y}\Big\{g(x)- c_1 \Big\|\nabla g(x)\Big\|^2\Big\}
-\inf_y\Big\{ h(y)-c_1 \|\nabla h(y)\|^2 \Big\},

where $r_1:= \epsilon_0c_3+\sigma-\|P\|^2c_1>0$
and $r_2:=\epsilon_0c_5-c_6>0$. 
By A2,  since $h$ is $L_h$ Lipschitz differentiable then for any $k\ge 1$ 
and $\delta>0$ we have

$

\big(\delta-\frac{L_h\delta^2}{2}\big)\|\nabla h(y^k)\|^2.
$
%

\begin{eqnarray}\label{hbd}

\end{eqnarray}

$\delta-\frac{L_h\delta^2}{2}=c_1$. By (\ref{hbd}), the right hand side of (\ref{thmbdd-eq1}) is finite
hence

\begin{eqnarray}\label{finite}
\sum_{i=1}^pf(x_i^{k})+\|{\bf Ax}^{k}+By^{k}+\alpha^{-1}z^{k}+b\|^2
+\|\Delta y^{k}\|^2 +\|\Delta z^k\|^2<+\infty.
\end{eqnarray}
%
By A1, since $f_i, i=1,\dots,p$ are coercive and $\sum_{i=1}^pf(x_i^{k})<+\infty$, then the sequence 
$\{x_i^k\}_{k\ge 0}$  is bounded for $i=1,\dots,p$, and so are 
$\{{\bf x}^k\}_{k\ge 0}$ and $\{{\bf Ax}^k\}_{k\ge 0}$.
%
%In addition, by (\ref{finite}) the sequences 
%$\{Ax^{k}+By^{k}+\alpha^{-1}z^{k}+c\}_{k\ge k_0}$ and $\{ \Delta y^{k}\}_{k\ge k_0}$ are bounded, 
%then $\{A\Delta x^k\}_{k\ge k_0}$ and $\{B\Delta y^k\}_{k\ge k_0}$
%are bounded which follows that $\{\Delta z^k\}_{k\ge 0}$ is bounded.

By the $z$ iterate of PADMM we have
$
By^{k} = \frac{1}{\alpha\beta} \Delta z^{k} -{\bf Ax}^{k}-b.
$
By (\ref{finite}), $\{\Delta z^k\}_{k\ge 0}$ is bounded.
By A3, $B\tr B$ is invertible, thus $\{y^k\}_{k\ge 0}$ is bounded.
Finally, by (\ref{finite}) $\{{\bf Ax}^{k}+By^{k}+\frac{1}{\alpha}z^{k}\}_{k\ge 0}$ is bounded
and ${\bf Ax}^k$ and $By^k$ are bounded, so 
$\{z^k\}_{k\ge 0}$ is then bounded.

Summing up (\ref{Lbarmon}) for $k=1,\dots, K-1$, $K\ge 2$ gives

\[
\sum_{k=1}^{K}
\Big\{\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k}\|^2
+\|\Delta y^{k}\|^2
+\|\Delta z^{k}\|^2\Big\}\le \frac{1}{\sigma}(\bar{\mathcal L}_1 - \bar{\mathcal L}_K) .
\]
Since $\{({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k)\}_{k\ge 0}$ is bounded, by Lemma \ref{thm1} (ii) the right hand side is finite for any $K$.
We let $K$ approach to infinity to obtain 
\begin{eqnarray*}

\Big\{\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k}\|^2 +\|\Delta y^{k}\|^2+\|\Delta z^{k}\|^2\Big\}<
\frac{1}{\sigma}(\bar{\mathcal L}_1 - \inf_{k\ge 1}\bar{\mathcal L}_k) <
+\infty.
\end{eqnarray*}
This follows 
$
\displaystyle{\lim_{k\to \infty}} \Big(\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k}\|^2 +\|\Delta y^{k}\|^2+\|\Delta z^{k}\|^2\Big)=0,
$
and consequently 
$
\displaystyle{\lim_{k\to \infty}} \|\Delta x_1^{k}\|
=\dots
=\displaystyle{\lim_{k\to \infty}} \|\Delta x_p^{k}\|
=
\displaystyle{\lim_{k\to \infty}}\|\Delta y^{k}\|
=
\displaystyle{\lim_{k\to \infty}}\|\Delta z^{k}\| =0.\quad\square
$

the error sequence 
$e_k:=\bar{\mathcal L}_k-\bar{\mathcal L}_*, k\ge 1$
is non-negative, monotonically decreasing, and converges to zero. 
We prove under two cases.

 {\it Case 1:} let assume that 
there is a $k_1\in\mathbb Z_+$ such that $e_{k_1}=0$. 
Since $\{e_k\}_{k\ge 1}$ is monotonically decreasing, 
$e_k=0$ for all $k\ge k_1$.
By Lemma \ref{thm1}(i) then we have
\[

 \frac{1}{\sigma}(e_k-e_{k+1})=0,\quad \forall k\ge k_1.

then

\Big\{\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k}\|
+\|\Delta y^{k}\|
+\|\Delta z^{k}\|\Big\}
=\sum_{k=1}^{k_1} \Big\{

+\|\Delta y^{k}\|

\] 
is bounded.

{\it Case 2:}
we let  $e_k>0$ for all $k\ge 1$. 
By Lemma \ref{thm1}(i) we have

%|||\Delta u^{k+1}|||^2=
\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|^2+\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|^2+\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|^2 \le 
 \frac{1}{\sigma}( e_k-e_{k+1}),\quad \forall k\ge 1.
\end{eqnarray}
%
By Lemma \ref{lma-cluster2}, $\Omega$ is nonempty, compact, and connected,
and $\bar{\mathcal L}$ takes on a constant value $\bar{\mathcal L}_*$ on $\Omega$. 
Since $\bar{\mathcal L}_{k}\searrow\bar{\mathcal L}_*$ as $k\to\infty$ and $\bar{\mathcal{L}}$ satisfies 
the {K\L} property then there exists  $ k_1\ge 1$ such that 
$\bar{\mathcal L}_*<\bar{\mathcal L}_k<\bar{\mathcal L}_*+\eta$
for all $k\ge k_1$ and some $\eta>0$.
%
Moreover, $\lim_{k\to\infty} {\rm dist} \big[ ({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k,y^{k-1},x^{k-1}), \Omega\big]=0$ by
Lemma \ref{lma-cluster2}, 
thus for a given $\epsilon>0$ there exists $k_2\ge 1$ such that for all $k\ge k_2$ it holds
\[
{\rm dist} \Big[ ({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k,y^{k-1},x^{k-1}), \Omega\Big]<\epsilon. 
\]
Let  $\tilde k:=\max\{ k_1,k_2,3 \}$, 
then $({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k,y^{k-1},x^{k-1})\in\mathcal S$
 and
%
$
\psi'(\bar{\mathcal L}_k-\bar{\mathcal L}_*)\cdot {\rm dist}\Big(0, 
\partial \bar{\mathcal L}_k \Big)
\ge 1$ for all $k\ge \tilde k$, or equivalently

\cdot {\rm dist}\Big(0, 
\partial \bar{\mathcal L}_k \Big)
 \ge1.
\end{eqnarray}
%
Multiply both sides of this inequality by $ |||\Delta u^{k+1}|||^2 $ to get
%
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:001}
 \psi'(e_{k}) \cdot {\rm dist}\Big(0, 
\partial \bar{\mathcal L}_k \Big) |||\Delta u^{k+1}|||^2 \ge |||\Delta u^{k+1}|||^2,
\end{eqnarray}
where 
$|||\Delta u^k|||^2=\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^k\|^2+\|\Delta y^k\|^2+\|\Delta z^k\|^2.$
%
By (\ref{s1}), (\ref{eq:001}) leads to 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:002}
 \frac {1}{\sigma} \psi'(e_{k}) (e_k-e_{k+1})\cdot {\rm dist}\Big(0, 
\partial \bar{\mathcal L}_k \Big)  \ge |||\Delta u^{k+1}|||^2.
\end{eqnarray}
%
By the concavity of $\psi$, $\psi(e_{k}) -\psi(e_{k+1})\ge  \psi'(e_{k}) (e_{k} - e_{k+1})$, hence
%
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:003}
|||\Delta u^{k+1}|||^2 \le 
 \frac{1}{\sigma} \big(\psi(e_{k}) -\psi(e_{k+1})\big) 
 \cdot {\rm dist}(0, \partial \bar{\mathcal L}_k ).
\end{eqnarray}
By the arithmetic mean-geometric mean inequality, for any $\gamma>0$ we  have
%
\begin{eqnarray}\label{artith-geo}
\sqrt{ \frac{1}{\sigma} \big(\psi(e_{k}) -\psi(e_{k+1})\big) 
 \cdot {\rm dist}(0, \partial \bar{\mathcal L}_k )}
 \le \frac{\gamma}{2\sigma}  \big(\psi(e_{k}) -\psi(e_{k+1})\big) 
+\frac{1}{2\gamma}{\rm dist}(0, \partial \bar{\mathcal L}_k ).
 \end{eqnarray}
%
Moreover,
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:004}
\frac{1}{\sqrt{p+2}} \Big(\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|\Big)
\le |||\Delta u^{k+1}|||.
\end{eqnarray}
%

%
\begin{eqnarray}\label{main}

+\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|
\le \frac{\gamma\sqrt{p+2}}{2\sigma}  
\big(\psi(e_{k}) -\psi(e_{k+1})\big)

\end{eqnarray}

defined in Lemma \ref{lma-D}, hence

\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:import}
\begin{array}{c}
\displaystyle{
\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|
}\\[.1in]
\le 
\displaystyle{
\frac{\gamma\sqrt{p+2}}{2\sigma}  
\big(\psi(e_{k}) -\psi(e_{k+1})\big) 
+
\frac{\tilde \rho\sqrt{p+2}}{2\gamma}
\Big(
\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k}\|
+\|\Delta y^{k}\|
+\|\Delta z^{k}\|\Big).
}
\end{array}
\end{eqnarray}
%
For any $K\ge k\ge \underline{k}$, the following identity holds
\[
\sum_{k=\underline k}^K\|\Delta w^{k}\| =
\sum_{k=\underline k}^{K}
\|\Delta w^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta w^{\underline k}\|-\|\Delta w^{K+1}\|.
\]

\begin{eqnarray*}

\Big\{\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|\Big\}
\le
\delta_1
\big(\psi(e_{\underline k}) -\psi(e_{K+1})\big) 
&\\
&
+\delta_2
\Big(
\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{\underline k}\|
+\|\Delta y^{\underline k}\|
+\|\Delta z^{\underline k}\|\Big)
-\delta_2
\Big(
\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{K+1}\|
+\|\Delta y^{K+1}\|
+\|\Delta z^{K+1}\|\Big),&
\end{eqnarray*}
where $\delta_1:={\gamma\sqrt{p+2}}/{2\sigma\delta_0} $ 
and 
$\delta_2= {\tilde \rho\sqrt{p+2}}/{2\gamma\delta_0}$.
%
Recall that $e_k$ is monotonically decreasing and
$\psi'>0$, therefore
%
\begin{eqnarray*}
&\sum_{k=\underline k}^K
\Big\{\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|
\Big\}\le  
\delta_1
\psi(e_{\underline k})
+\delta_2\big(
\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{\underline k}\|
+\|\Delta y^{\underline k}\|
+\|\Delta z^{\underline k}\|\big).
&
\end{eqnarray*}
%
The right hand side of this inequality is bounded for any $K\ge \underline k$, we let $K\to\infty$ to obtain
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:0005}
\sum_{k=\underline k}^{\infty}
\Big(\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|
\Big)
\le 
\delta_1
\psi(e_{\underline k})
+\delta_2
\Big(
\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{\underline k}\|
+\|\Delta y^{\underline k}\|
+\|\Delta z^{\underline k}\|\Big).
\end{eqnarray}
%
Then (\ref{eq:0005}) together with the fact that $\{({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k)\}_{k\ge 0}$ is  bounded gives
%
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:000000005}
\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}
\Big\{\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|
\Big\}
<+\infty.
\end{eqnarray}


For any $p,q,K\in\mathbb Z_+$ where $q\ge p$ we have 
\begin{eqnarray*}
|||u^q-u^p||| =||| \sum_{k=p}^{q-1} \Delta u^{k+1}|||
\le
 \sum_{k=p}^{q-1} |||\Delta u^{k+1}|||
 \le 
\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}|||\Delta u^{k+1}|||.
\end{eqnarray*}
%
Since by (\ref{eq:000000005}) the right hand side is finite 
then 
\[
\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}|||\Delta u^{k+1}|||
\le \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}
\Big\{\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|
\Big\}
<+\infty.
\]
This implies that $\{u^k\}_{k\ge 0}=\{({\bf x}, y^k,z^k)\}_{k\ge 0}$ is a Cauchy sequence. 
By Lemma \ref{thm-cluster} it converges to a stationary point.  $\square$

Let $\Phi:\mathbb R^d\to \bar{\mathbb R}$ be a proper and lower semicontinuous function. 
 The domain  of $\Phi$, denoted ${\rm dom}\; \Phi$, is defined by 
${\rm dom}\; \Phi:=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\; \Phi(x)<+\infty\}.
$
%
%The graph of the $\Phi$, denoted  ${\rm Graph}\; \Phi$, defined by
%$
% {\rm Graph}\; \Phi:=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^d \times\mathbb R: y=\Phi(x)\}.
%$
For any $x\in {\rm dom}\; \Phi$, the {\it Fr\'echet (viscosity) subdifferential} of $\Phi$ at $x$,
denoted $\hat\partial\Phi(x)$, is defined by
\[
\hat\partial\Phi(x)=
\Big\{
s\in\mathbb R^d: \;\;\lim_{y\neq x}\inf_{y\to x} \frac{\Phi(y)-\Phi(x)-\langle s, y-x\rangle}{\|y-x\|}\ge 0
\Big\}.
\]
For $x\notin {\rm dom}\;\Phi$, then $\hat\partial\Phi (x)=\emptyset$.
The {\it limiting (Mordukhovich) subdifferential}, or simply the subdifferential for short,
 of $\Phi$ at $x\in {\rm dom}\;\Phi$, denoted $\partial\Phi(x)$, is defined by
 %
\begin{eqnarray*}
\partial\Phi(x):=\{s\in\mathbb R^d: \exists x^k\to x,\;\Phi(x^k)\to\Phi(x)\;\;
{\rm and} \;\; s^k\in\hat\Phi(x^k)\to s\;\;{\rm as}\; k\to+\infty\}.
\end{eqnarray*}

Let $(x^k,s^k)\in {\rm Graph}\; \partial\Phi:=\{(x,s)\in\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d: s\in\partial \Phi(x)\}.
$
Let $(x^k,s^k)\to (x^*,s^*)$ as $k\to\infty$. Since $s^k\in\partial \Phi(x^k)$, 
and $\Phi(x^k)\to \Phi(x^*)$ as $k\to\infty$ we have  $(x^*,s^*)\in {\rm Graph}\; \partial\Phi$.
The well-known Fermat's rule ``$x\in\mathbb R^d$ is a local minimizer of $\Phi$, then $\partial \Phi(x)\ni 0$''
remains unchanged. If $x\in\mathbb R^d$ such that $\partial \Phi(x)\ni 0$ the point $x$ is called 
a critical point. We denote by ${\rm crit}\; \Phi$ the set of {\it critical points} of $\Phi$,
that is 
$
{\rm crit}\; \Phi=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:0\in\partial\Phi(x)\}.
$

Let $\Omega$ be a subset of $\mathbb R^d$  and $x$ is any point in $\mathbb R^d$. The distance from $x$
to $\Omega$, denoted ${\rm dist}(x,\Omega)$, is defined by 
${\rm dist}(x,\Omega)=\inf\{\|x-z\|:\;z\in\Omega\}$, and the set of points in $\Omega$ that 
achieve this infimum (the projection of $x$ onto $\Omega$) is defined by ${\rm Proj}_{\Omega}(x)$.
The set ${\rm Proj}_{\Omega}(x)$ becomes a singleton if $\Omega$ is a closed convex 
set. If $\Omega=\emptyset$, then ${\rm dist}(x,\Omega)=+\infty$ for all $x\in\mathbb R^d$. 
For any real-valued function $\Phi$ on $\mathbb R^d$ we have
\[
{\rm dist}(0,\partial\Phi(x))=\inf\{\|s^*\|: \; s^*\in\partial \Phi(x)\}.
\]  
%
Let $F:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\to \bar{\mathbb R}$ be a lower semicontinuous function. The subdifferentiation of $F$ at the point $(\hat x,\hat y)$ is defined by 
$
\partial F(\hat x, \hat y)=\big(\partial_x F(\hat x,\hat y), \partial_y F(\hat x,\hat y)\big),
$
where $\partial_x F$ and $\partial_y F$ are respectively the differential of the function 
$F(\cdot,y)$ when $y\in\mathbb R^m$ is fixed, and $F(x,\cdot)$ when $x$ is fixed.

it holds

\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:thm1KL}
\psi'\Big(\bar{\mathcal L}(v)-\bar{\mathcal L}(v^*)\Big) \cdot

 Then $\{u^k\}_{k\ge 0}:=\{({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k)\}_{k\ge 0}$
 satisfies

+ \| \Delta y^{k}\|
+ \| \Delta z^{k}\|\Big\}<+\infty,

\begin{proof}
By Lemma \ref{thm1}, the sequence $\{\bar{\mathcal L}_k\}_{k\ge 1}$ is monotonically
 decreasing and converges. Let $\bar{\mathcal L}_*:=\lim_{k\to\infty}\bar{\mathcal L}_k$, then 
the error sequence 
$e_k:=\bar{\mathcal L}_k-\bar{\mathcal L}_*, k\ge 1$
is non-negative, monotonically decreasing, and converges to zero. 
We prove under two cases.

 {\it Case 1:} let assume that 
there is a $k_1\in\mathbb Z_+$ such that $e_{k_1}=0$. 
Since $\{e_k\}_{k\ge 1}$ is monotonically decreasing, 
$e_k=0$ for all $k\ge k_1$.
By Lemma \ref{thm1}(i) then we have
\[
\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|^2+\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|^2+\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|^2 \le 
 \frac{1}{\sigma}(e_k-e_{k+1})=0,\quad \forall k\ge k_1.
\]
Hence  as $\{({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k)\}_{k\ge 0}$ is a bounded sequence
then 
\[
\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}
\Big\{\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k}\|
+\|\Delta y^{k}\|
+\|\Delta z^{k}\|\Big\}
=\sum_{k=1}^{k_1} \Big\{
\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k}\|
+\|\Delta y^{k}\|
+\|\Delta z^{k}\|\Big\}
\] 
is bounded.

{\it Case 2:}
we let  $e_k>0$ for all $k\ge 1$. 
By Lemma \ref{thm1}(i) we have
%
\begin{eqnarray}\label{s1}
%|||\Delta u^{k+1}|||^2=
\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|^2+\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|^2+\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|^2 \le 
 \frac{1}{\sigma}( e_k-e_{k+1}),\quad \forall k\ge 1.
\end{eqnarray}
%
By Lemma \ref{lma-cluster2}, $\Omega$ is nonempty, compact, and connected,
and $\bar{\mathcal L}$ takes on a constant value $\bar{\mathcal L}_*$ on $\Omega$. 
Since $\bar{\mathcal L}_{k}\searrow\bar{\mathcal L}_*$ as $k\to\infty$ and $\bar{\mathcal{L}}$ satisfies 
the {K\L} property then there exists  $ k_1\ge 1$ such that 
$\bar{\mathcal L}_*<\bar{\mathcal L}_k<\bar{\mathcal L}_*+\eta$
for all $k\ge k_1$ and some $\eta>0$.
%
Moreover, $\lim_{k\to\infty} {\rm dist} \big[ ({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k,y^{k-1},x^{k-1}), \Omega\big]=0$ by
Lemma \ref{lma-cluster2}, 
thus for a given $\epsilon>0$ there exists $k_2\ge 1$ such that for all $k\ge k_2$ it holds
\[
{\rm dist} \Big[ ({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k,y^{k-1},x^{k-1}), \Omega\Big]<\epsilon. 
\]
Let  $\tilde k:=\max\{ k_1,k_2,3 \}$, 
then $({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k,y^{k-1},x^{k-1})\in\mathcal S$
 and
%
$
\psi'(\bar{\mathcal L}_k-\bar{\mathcal L}_*)\cdot {\rm dist}\Big(0, 
\partial \bar{\mathcal L}_k \Big)
\ge 1$ for all $k\ge \tilde k$, or equivalently
%
\begin{eqnarray}\label{KL}
\psi'(e_k)
\cdot {\rm dist}\Big(0, 
\partial \bar{\mathcal L}_k \Big)
 \ge1.
\end{eqnarray}
%
Multiply both sides of this inequality by $ |||\Delta u^{k+1}|||^2 $ to get
%
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:001}
 \psi'(e_{k}) \cdot {\rm dist}\Big(0, 
\partial \bar{\mathcal L}_k \Big) |||\Delta u^{k+1}|||^2 \ge |||\Delta u^{k+1}|||^2,
\end{eqnarray}
where 
$|||\Delta u^k|||^2=\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^k\|^2+\|\Delta y^k\|^2+\|\Delta z^k\|^2.$
%
By (\ref{s1}), (\ref{eq:001}) leads to 
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:002}
 \frac {1}{\sigma} \psi'(e_{k}) (e_k-e_{k+1})\cdot {\rm dist}\Big(0, 
\partial \bar{\mathcal L}_k \Big)  \ge |||\Delta u^{k+1}|||^2.
\end{eqnarray}
%
By the concavity of $\psi$, $\psi(e_{k}) -\psi(e_{k+1})\ge  \psi'(e_{k}) (e_{k} - e_{k+1})$, hence
%
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:003}
|||\Delta u^{k+1}|||^2 \le 
 \frac{1}{\sigma} \big(\psi(e_{k}) -\psi(e_{k+1})\big) 
 \cdot {\rm dist}(0, \partial \bar{\mathcal L}_k ).
\end{eqnarray}
By the arithmetic mean-geometric mean inequality, for any $\gamma>0$ we  have
%
\begin{eqnarray}\label{artith-geo}
\sqrt{ \frac{1}{\sigma} \big(\psi(e_{k}) -\psi(e_{k+1})\big) 
 \cdot {\rm dist}(0, \partial \bar{\mathcal L}_k )}
 \le \frac{\gamma}{2\sigma}  \big(\psi(e_{k}) -\psi(e_{k+1})\big) 
+\frac{1}{2\gamma}{\rm dist}(0, \partial \bar{\mathcal L}_k ).
 \end{eqnarray}
%
Moreover,
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:004}
\frac{1}{\sqrt{p+2}} \Big(\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|\Big)
\le |||\Delta u^{k+1}|||.
\end{eqnarray}
%
Thus  (\ref{eq:003}), (\ref{artith-geo}), and (\ref{eq:004}) give rise to
%
\begin{eqnarray}\label{main}
\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|
\le \frac{\gamma\sqrt{p+2}}{2\sigma}  
\big(\psi(e_{k}) -\psi(e_{k+1})\big) 
+\frac{\sqrt{p+2}}{2\gamma}{\rm dist}(0, \partial \bar{\mathcal L}_k ).
\end{eqnarray}
%
Note that ${\rm dist}(0, \partial \bar{\mathcal L}_k)=|||s^k|||$, where $s^k\in\partial \bar{\mathcal L}_k$ 
defined in Lemma \ref{lma-D}, hence 
%
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:import}
\begin{array}{c}
\displaystyle{
\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|
}\\[.1in]
\le 
\displaystyle{
\frac{\gamma\sqrt{p+2}}{2\sigma}  
\big(\psi(e_{k}) -\psi(e_{k+1})\big) 
+
\frac{\tilde \rho\sqrt{p+2}}{2\gamma}
\Big(
\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k}\|
+\|\Delta y^{k}\|
+\|\Delta z^{k}\|\Big).
}
\end{array}
\end{eqnarray}
%
For any $K\ge k\ge \underline{k}$, the following identity holds
\[
\sum_{k=\underline k}^K\|\Delta w^{k}\| =
\sum_{k=\underline k}^{K}
\|\Delta w^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta w^{\underline k}\|-\|\Delta w^{K+1}\|.
\]
Choose $\gamma>0$ large enough such that $2\gamma>\tilde \rho\sqrt{p+2}$.
Let $\delta_0=1-\frac{\tilde \rho\sqrt{p+2}}{2\gamma}>0$.
%
Summing up (\ref{eq:import}) from $k=\underline k\ge \tilde k $ to $K\ge \underline k$ leads to
\begin{eqnarray*}
&\sum_{k=\underline k}^K
\Big\{\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|\Big\}
\le
\delta_1
\big(\psi(e_{\underline k}) -\psi(e_{K+1})\big) 
&\\
&
+\delta_2
\Big(
\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{\underline k}\|
+\|\Delta y^{\underline k}\|
+\|\Delta z^{\underline k}\|\Big)
-\delta_2
\Big(
\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{K+1}\|
+\|\Delta y^{K+1}\|
+\|\Delta z^{K+1}\|\Big),&
\end{eqnarray*}
where $\delta_1:={\gamma\sqrt{p+2}}/{2\sigma\delta_0} $ 
and 
$\delta_2= {\tilde \rho\sqrt{p+2}}/{2\gamma\delta_0}$.
%
Recall that $e_k$ is monotonically decreasing and
$\psi'>0$, therefore
%
\begin{eqnarray*}
&\sum_{k=\underline k}^K
\Big\{\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|
\Big\}\le  
\delta_1
\psi(e_{\underline k})
+\delta_2\big(
\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{\underline k}\|
+\|\Delta y^{\underline k}\|
+\|\Delta z^{\underline k}\|\big).
&
\end{eqnarray*}
%
The right hand side of this inequality is bounded for any $K\ge \underline k$, we let $K\to\infty$ to obtain
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:0005}
\sum_{k=\underline k}^{\infty}
\Big(\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|
\Big)
\le 
\delta_1
\psi(e_{\underline k})
+\delta_2
\Big(
\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{\underline k}\|
+\|\Delta y^{\underline k}\|
+\|\Delta z^{\underline k}\|\Big).
\end{eqnarray}
%
Then (\ref{eq:0005}) together with the fact that $\{({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k)\}_{k\ge 0}$ is  bounded gives
%
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:000000005}
\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}
\Big\{\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|
\Big\}
<+\infty.
\end{eqnarray}


For any $p,q,K\in\mathbb Z_+$ where $q\ge p$ we have 
\begin{eqnarray*}
|||u^q-u^p||| =||| \sum_{k=p}^{q-1} \Delta u^{k+1}|||
\le
 \sum_{k=p}^{q-1} |||\Delta u^{k+1}|||
 \le 
\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}|||\Delta u^{k+1}|||.
\end{eqnarray*}
%
Since by (\ref{eq:000000005}) the right hand side is finite 
then 
\[
\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}|||\Delta u^{k+1}|||
\le \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}
\Big\{\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|
+\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|
\Big\}
<+\infty.
\]
This implies that $\{u^k\}_{k\ge 0}=\{({\bf x}, y^k,z^k)\}_{k\ge 0}$ is a Cauchy sequence. 
By Lemma \ref{thm-cluster} it converges to a stationary point.  $\square$
 \end{proof}

and evaluating the result at the point $({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k})$ yields

 \end{eqnarray}

\begin{proof}
Let $\{({\bf x}^{k_j},y^{k_j},z^{k_j})\}_{j\ge 0}$ be a subsequence of the sequence 
$\{({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k})\}_{j\ge 0}$
generated by the PADMM algorithm such that
$\lim_{j\to\infty} ({\bf x}^{k_j},y^{k_j},z^{k_j})=({\bf x}^*, y^*, z^*).$
By A1, for $i=1,\dots,p$ the functions $f_i$ are lower semicontinuous hence

\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:flsc0}
f_i(x_i^*)\le \lim\inf_{j\to\infty} f(x_i^{k_j}).
\end{eqnarray}
%
By the $x_i$-subproblem of the PADMM algorithm for any $v\in\mathbb R^{n_i}$ we have 
\[
\mathcal L^{\alpha} (x_{<i}^{k_j+1},x_i^{k_j+1}, x^{k_j}_{>i}, y^{k_j},z^{k_j})+
\frac{1}{2}\|\Delta x_i^{k_j+1}\|_{Q_i}^2
\le \mathcal L^{\alpha} (x_{<i}^{k_j+1},v, x^{k_j}_{>i}, y^{k_j},z^{k_j})
+\frac{1}{2}\|v- x_i^{k_j}\|_{Q_i}^2.
\]
We choose $v=x_i^*$ and exploit the cosine rule
$\|a_1+c\|^2-\|a_2+c\|^2=\|a_2-a_1\|^2+2\langle a_2+c, a_2-a_1\rangle$
with 
$a_1=A_ix_i^*$, $a_2=A_ix_i^{k_j+1}$ 
and $c=A_{<i}x_{<i}^{k_j+1}+A_{>i}x^{k_j}_{>i}+By^{k_j}+b$ to obtain
 %
\begin{eqnarray*}
&f_i(x_i^{k_j+1})- f_i(x_i^*) +
\langle A_i\tr z^{k_j},x^{k_j+1}_i-x_i^*\rangle+\|\Delta x_i^{k_j+1}\|^2_{Q_i} 
\le 
\frac{\alpha}{2}\|A_i (x_i^{k_j+1}-x_i^*)\|^2&
\\
&+\alpha \Big\langle A_i (x_i^*-x_i^{k_j+1}), A_{<i}x^{k_j+1}_{<i}+A_ix_i^{k_j+1}+A_{>i}x_{>i}^{k_j}+By^{k_j}+b\Big\rangle.
&
\end{eqnarray*}
%
Since $\{({\bf x}^{k_j},y^{k_j},z^{k_j})\}_{j\ge 0}$  is a convergent sequence, 
 it is bounded and the difference of consequtive terms approaches  zero. 
Thus the latter inequality reduces to 
$\displaystyle{\lim\sup_{j\to \infty}} f_i(x_i^{k_j+1})-f_i(x_i^*)\le 0$ and 
in view of (\ref{eq:flsc0}) we then have
$
\lim_{j\to \infty} f_i(x_i^{k_j})=f_i(x_i^*),
$
which follows that
$
\lim_{j\to \infty} \sum_{i=1}^p f_i(x_i^{k_j})=\sum_{i=1}^p f_i(x_i^*).
$
%
By A2, $h(y)$ is smooth hence $\lim_{j\to\infty} h(y^{k_j})= h(y^*)$.
Clearly, ${\bf Ax}^{k_j}+By^{k_j}+b\to {\bf Ax}^{*}+By^{*}+b$
as $j\to\infty$.
Thus $\displaystyle{\lim_{j\to\infty}} \mathcal L^{\alpha} ({\bf x}^{k_j},y^{k_j},z^{k_j})
= \mathcal L^{\alpha} ({\bf x}^*, y^*, z^*).$ $\quad\square$
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}
{\bf (i)} Let $k\in\mathbb Z_+$ and $i\in\{1,\dots,p\}$ be fixed.
By the $x_i$ subproblem we have
\[
\mathcal L^{\alpha}(x_{<i}^{k+1},x_i^{k}, x^{k}_{>i},y^k,z^k)-
\mathcal L^{\alpha}(x_{<i}^{k+1},x_i^{k+1}, x^{k}_{>i},y^k,z^k)
\ge \|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|_{Q_i}^2.
\]
%
On the other hand, by the optimality condition of $x_i$-sub-minimization problem we have 
$ \bar{d_i}\in\partial f_i(x_i^{k+1})$
where 
\[
\bar{d_i}:=-A_i \tr z^k-
\alpha A_i\tr \big(A_{<i} x_{<i}^{k+1}+A_ix_i^{k+1}+A_{>i}x_{>i}^k+By^k+b
\big).
\]
By this we then have
\begin{eqnarray*}
&\mathcal L^{\alpha}(x_{<i}^{k+1},x_i^k, x^{k}_{>i},y^k,z^k)-
\mathcal L^{\alpha}(x_{<i}^{k+1},x_i^{k+1}, x^{k}_{>i},y^k,z^k)& \\[.1in]
&=f_i(x_i^k)-f_i(x_i^{k+1})
+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|A_i\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|^2-\langle \bar{d_i}, \Delta x_i^{k+1}\rangle&
\\[.1in]
&\ge \frac{\alpha}{2}\|A_i\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|^2
- \frac{\epsilon_i}{2}\|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|^2
=\frac 12 \|\Delta x_i^{k+1}\|_{\alpha A_i\tr A_i-\epsilon_iI}^2.&
\end{eqnarray*}

%%%%
{\bf (ii)}
Let $k\ge 0$ be fixed. From the optimality condition of $y$ minimization problem 
we have
\begin{eqnarray*}
\nabla h(y^{k+1})+\alpha B\tr ({\bf Ax}^{k+1}+By^{k+1}+b)
+B\tr z^k+P \Delta y^{k+1}=0.
\end{eqnarray*}
Multiply this equation by $\Delta y^{k+1}$ and rearrange to obtain
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq:2}
- \alpha\big\langle B\tr ({\bf Ax}^{k+1}+ By^{k+1}+b),\Delta y^{k+1}\big\rangle 
-\langle B\tr z^k, \Delta y^{k+1}\rangle
=\langle \nabla h(y^{k+1}),\Delta y^{k+1}\rangle +\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|_P^2.
\end{eqnarray}
By this and the fact that $h(y)$ is $L_h$ Lipschitz continuous we then get 
%
\begin{eqnarray*}
&\mathcal L^{\alpha}(x^{k+1},y^k,z^k)-\mathcal L^{\alpha}(x^{k+1},y^{k+1},z^{k})&
\\[.1in]
&= h(y^k)-h(y^{k+1})
+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|{\bf Ax}^{k+1}+By^k+b\|^2
-\frac{\alpha}{2}\|{\bf Ax}^{k+1}+By^{k+1}+b\|^2
-\langle B\tr z^k, \Delta y^{k+1} \rangle&
\\[.1in]
 &=h(y^k)-h(y^{k+1})
+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|B\Delta y^{k+1}\|^2
-\alpha \langle \Delta y^{k+1}, B\tr ({\bf Ax}^{k+1}+By^{k+1}+b)\rangle 
-\langle B\tr z^k, \Delta y^{k+1} \rangle&
\\[.1in]
&=h(y^k)-h(y^{k+1})
+\langle \nabla h(y^{k+1}),\Delta y^{k+1}\rangle +\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|_P^2
+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|B\Delta y^{k+1}\|^2
&\\[.1in]
&\ge\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|_P^2
+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|B\Delta y^{k+1}\|^2
-\frac{L_h}{2}\|\Delta y^{k+1}\|^2 = 
\frac{1}{2} \|\Delta y^{k+1}\|_{D}^2.&
\end{eqnarray*}
%
%
{\bf (iii)} By the $z$ iterate of the algorithm we obtain
\begin{eqnarray*}
&\mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^{k+1},y^{k+1}, z^k)-
\mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^{k+1},y^{k+1},z^{k+1})=
\langle z^k-z^{k+1}, {\bf Ax}^{k+1}+By^{k+1}+b\rangle
=-\frac{1}{\alpha\beta}\|\Delta z^{k+1}\|^2.&
\end{eqnarray*}
%
That completes the proof. $\square$
\end{proof}

where

\|{\bf Q}\|+\|{\bf A}\|^2,\;
\|P\|+\alpha \|{\bf A}\|\|B\|+4\epsilon_0c_3, \;
\|{\bf A}\|  +\|B\|+4\epsilon_0c_5\|B\|^2 + \frac{1}{\alpha\beta}\Big\},

\begin{proof}
Let $k\ge 1$ be fixed and $(\{d_{x_i}^{k}\}_{i=1}^p, d_y^{k}, d_z^{k})\in \partial \mathcal L^{\alpha}(x^k,y^k,z^k)$. By taking partial derivatives of $\bar{\mathcal L}$ with respect to $x,y,z,y',z'$ and evaluating 
them at $({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k,y^{k-1},z^{k-1})$ we obtain
%
\begin{eqnarray*}
%s_{x_i}^{k}&:=& 
\partial_{x_i} \bar{\mathcal L}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k},y^{k-1},z^{k-1})
&=&\partial_{x_i} \mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k})
\ni d_{x_i}^{k},\; i=1,\dots,p;\\
%s_y^{k}&:=&
\nabla_y  \bar{\mathcal L} ({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k},y^{k-1},z^{k-1})
&=&\nabla_y \mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k})
+2\epsilon_0c_3 \Delta y^k=
d_y^{k}+2\epsilon_0c_3 \Delta y^k;\\
%s_z^{k}&:=&
\nabla_z  \bar{\mathcal L}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k},y^{k-1},z^{k-1})
&=&\nabla_z \mathcal L^{\alpha}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k})
+2\epsilon_0c_5 BB\tr \Delta z^{k}=
d_z^{k}
+2\epsilon_0c_5 BB\tr\Delta z^{k};\\
%s_{y'}^{k}&:=&
\nabla_{y'}  \bar{\mathcal L}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k},y^{k-1},z^{k-1})
&=&-2\epsilon_0c_3\Delta y^k;\\
%d_{z'}^{k}&:=&
\nabla_{z'}  \bar{\mathcal L}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k},y^{k-1},z^{k-1})
&=&-2\epsilon_0c_5BB\tr \Delta z^k.
\end{eqnarray*}
%
These equations follow that 
\begin{eqnarray*}
s^k =
\left[
\begin{array}{c}
s^k_{x_1}\\
\vdots\\
s^k_{x_p}\\
s^k_{y} \\ 
s^k_{z}\\
s^k_{y'}\\
s^k_{z'}
\end{array}
\right]
=
\left[
\begin{array}{l}
d^k_{x_1}\\
\vdots\\[.1in]
d^k_{x_p}\\
d_y^{k}+2\epsilon_0c_3 \Delta y^k \\ 
d_z^{k}+2\epsilon_0c_5 BB\tr\Delta z^{k}\\
-2\epsilon_0c_3\Delta y^k\\
-2\epsilon_0c_5BB\tr \Delta z^k
\end{array}
\right]\in \partial \bar{\mathcal L}({\bf x}^{k},y^{k},z^{k},y^{k-1},z^{k-1}).
\end{eqnarray*} 
%
By the triangle inequality we have
%
\begin{eqnarray*}
&\|s_y^{k}\|\le \|d^{k}_y\|+2\epsilon_0c_3\|\Delta y^k\|,\quad\quad
\|s_z^{k}\|\le\|d^{k}_z\|+2\epsilon_0c_5\|B\|^2 \|\Delta z^k\|,&\\
&\|s_{y'}^{k}\|\le 2\epsilon_0c_3\|\Delta y^k\|,\quad\quad
\|s_z^{k}\|\le 2\epsilon_0c_5 \|B\|^2 \|\Delta z^k\|.&
\end{eqnarray*}
%
Thus
\begin{eqnarray*}
|||s^{k}|||&\le&  \sum_{i=1}^p\|s_{x_i}^{k}\|+\|s_y^{k}\|+\|s_z^{k}\|+ \|s_{y'}^{k}\|+\|s_z^{k}\|\\
&\le& \sum_{i=1}^p \|d^{k}_{x_i}\|+  \|d^{k}_y\|+\|d^{k}_z\|+
4\epsilon_0c_3\|\Delta y^{k}\|+
4\epsilon_0c_5 \|B\|^2 \|\Delta z^k\|.
\end{eqnarray*}
%
By Lemma \ref{thm-d}, we have 
%
\begin{eqnarray*}
&|||s^{k}|||\le
\Big(\|{\bf Q}\|+\|{\bf A}\|^2\Big) \sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k}\|
+\Big(\|P\|+\alpha \|{\bf A}\|\|B\| +4\epsilon_0c_3 \Big)      \|\Delta y^{k}\|&\\
&+\Big(\|{\bf A}\|  +\|B\|+4\epsilon_0c_5\|B\|^2+\frac{1}{\alpha\beta}\Big)  \|\Delta z^{k}\|
\le \tilde\rho \Big( \sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k}\|+   \|\Delta y^{k}\|+  \|\Delta z^{k}\|\Big). \quad \square&
\end{eqnarray*}

\end{proof}

source_units.raw_tex:
\begin{proof}
Let $\{({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k)\}_{k\ge 0}$ be a sequence generated by the PADMM algorithm.
%
By $\sigma>0$, the sequence $\{\bar{\mathcal L}_k\}_{k\ge 1}$ 
defined in (\ref{Lbark}) is monotonically decreasing, hence it is upper bounded by 
$\bar{\mathcal L}_1=\bar{\mathcal L}({\bf x}^1,y^1,z^1,y^0,z^0)$.
This follows that 
%
\begin{eqnarray}\label{ineq10}
\begin{array}{c}
\sum_{i=1}^pf(x_i^{k})+h(y^{k})
+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|{\bf Ax}^{k}+By^{k}
+\alpha^{-1}z^{k}+b\|^2-\frac{1}{2\alpha}\|z^{k}\|^2
\\[.1in]
+\sigma \sum_{i=1}^p \|\Delta x_i^{k}\|^2
 +\sigma\|\Delta z^{k}\|^2
+(\sigma+\epsilon_0c_3) \|\Delta y^{k}\|^2
+\epsilon_0c_5\|B\tr \Delta z^{k}\|^2
\le \bar{\mathcal L}_1
 \end{array}
\end{eqnarray}
%
for all $k\in\mathbb Z_+$.
By Lemma \ref{bounddual} (iii), (\ref{ineq10}) leads to 
%
\begin{eqnarray}\label{thmbdd-eq1}
\begin{array}{c}
\sum_{i=1}^pf(x_i^{k})+\frac{\alpha}{2}\|{\bf Ax}^{k}+By^{k}+\alpha^{-1}z^{k}+b\|^2
+r_1\|\Delta y^{k}\|^2\\[.1in]
+ \sigma\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x^{k}\|^2
+ r_2\|B\tr \Delta z^{k}\|^2
+\sigma\|\Delta z^{k}\|^2
\le\bar{\mathcal L}_1
%- \inf_{x,y}\Big\{g(x)- c_1 \Big\|\nabla g(x)\Big\|^2\Big\}
-\inf_y\Big\{ h(y)-c_1 \|\nabla h(y)\|^2 \Big\},
\end{array}
\end{eqnarray}
%
where $r_1:= \epsilon_0c_3+\sigma-\|P\|^2c_1>0$
and $r_2:=\epsilon_0c_5-c_6>0$. 
By A2,  since $h$ is $L_h$ Lipschitz differentiable then for any $k\ge 1$ 
and $\delta>0$ we have
%
$
h\big(y^k-\delta \nabla h(y^k)\big)\le h(y^k)- 
\big(\delta-\frac{L_h\delta^2}{2}\big)\|\nabla h(y^k)\|^2.
$
%
Again by A2, $h$ is bounded from below then
%
\begin{eqnarray}\label{hbd}
-\infty<\inf\{h(y)- \Big(\delta-\frac{L_h\delta^2}{2}\Big)\|\nabla h(y)\|^2: \; y\in\mathbb R^q\}.
\end{eqnarray}
%
We choose $\delta (>0)$ such that 
$\delta-\frac{L_h\delta^2}{2}=c_1$. By (\ref{hbd}), the right hand side of (\ref{thmbdd-eq1}) is finite
hence
%
\begin{eqnarray}\label{finite}
\sum_{i=1}^pf(x_i^{k})+\|{\bf Ax}^{k}+By^{k}+\alpha^{-1}z^{k}+b\|^2
+\|\Delta y^{k}\|^2 +\|\Delta z^k\|^2<+\infty.
\end{eqnarray}
%
By A1, since $f_i, i=1,\dots,p$ are coercive and $\sum_{i=1}^pf(x_i^{k})<+\infty$, then the sequence 
$\{x_i^k\}_{k\ge 0}$  is bounded for $i=1,\dots,p$, and so are 
$\{{\bf x}^k\}_{k\ge 0}$ and $\{{\bf Ax}^k\}_{k\ge 0}$.
%
%In addition, by (\ref{finite}) the sequences 
%$\{Ax^{k}+By^{k}+\alpha^{-1}z^{k}+c\}_{k\ge k_0}$ and $\{ \Delta y^{k}\}_{k\ge k_0}$ are bounded, 
%then $\{A\Delta x^k\}_{k\ge k_0}$ and $\{B\Delta y^k\}_{k\ge k_0}$
%are bounded which follows that $\{\Delta z^k\}_{k\ge 0}$ is bounded.

By the $z$ iterate of PADMM we have
$
By^{k} = \frac{1}{\alpha\beta} \Delta z^{k} -{\bf Ax}^{k}-b.
$
By (\ref{finite}), $\{\Delta z^k\}_{k\ge 0}$ is bounded.
By A3, $B\tr B$ is invertible, thus $\{y^k\}_{k\ge 0}$ is bounded.
Finally, by (\ref{finite}) $\{{\bf Ax}^{k}+By^{k}+\frac{1}{\alpha}z^{k}\}_{k\ge 0}$ is bounded
and ${\bf Ax}^k$ and $By^k$ are bounded, so 
$\{z^k\}_{k\ge 0}$ is then bounded.
%
Summing up (\ref{Lbarmon}) for $k=1,\dots, K-1$, $K\ge 2$ gives
%
\[
\sum_{k=1}^{K}
\Big\{\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k}\|^2
+\|\Delta y^{k}\|^2
+\|\Delta z^{k}\|^2\Big\}\le \frac{1}{\sigma}(\bar{\mathcal L}_1 - \bar{\mathcal L}_K) .
\]
Since $\{({\bf x}^k,y^k,z^k)\}_{k\ge 0}$ is bounded, by Lemma \ref{thm1} (ii) the right hand side is finite for any $K$.
We let $K$ approach to infinity to obtain 
\begin{eqnarray*}
\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}
\Big\{\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k}\|^2 +\|\Delta y^{k}\|^2+\|\Delta z^{k}\|^2\Big\}<
\frac{1}{\sigma}(\bar{\mathcal L}_1 - \inf_{k\ge 1}\bar{\mathcal L}_k) <
+\infty.
\end{eqnarray*}
This follows 
$
\displaystyle{\lim_{k\to \infty}} \Big(\sum_{i=1}^p\|\Delta x_i^{k}\|^2 +\|\Delta y^{k}\|^2+\|\Delta z^{k}\|^2\Big)=0,
$
and consequently 
$
\displaystyle{\lim_{k\to \infty}} \|\Delta x_1^{k}\|
=\dots
=\displaystyle{\lim_{k\to \infty}} \|\Delta x_p^{k}\|
=
\displaystyle{\lim_{k\to \infty}}\|\Delta y^{k}\|
=
\displaystyle{\lim_{k\to \infty}}\|\Delta z^{k}\| =0.\quad\square
$


\end{proof}
